title: Executive cyber security accountability
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: The board of directors or executive committee is accountable for cyber security.

title: Executive artificial intelligence accountability
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: The board of directors or executive committee is accountable for ensuring that artificial intelligence is secure, controllable, human-supervised and used in an ethical and accountable manner.

title: Cyber security leadership
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: A chief information security officer provides leadership and oversight of cyber security activities and delivers regular and timely risk-based reporting to the board of directors or executive committee on their organisation’s cyber security posture, the effectiveness of controls, current security risks and emerging cyber threats.

title: Cyber security resourcing
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Suitable and sufficient personnel and resources are identified, acquired and maintained in support of cyber security activities.

title: Security risk management responsibilities
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Security risk management responsibilities for an organisation and their suppliers, partners and customers, including any shared responsibilities, are documented and communicated to all relevant parties with accountability arrangements in place to ensure their effective implementation.

title: Security risk management assurance
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Security risk management activities for an organisation and their systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are embedded into organisational risk management frameworks and subject to ongoing monitoring and assurance activities by the board of directors or executive committee.

title: Security risk acceptance
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Residual security risks for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data), including inherited and shared security risks, are accepted before they are authorised for use and continuously monitored and managed throughout their operational life.

title: Security risk communication
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Residual security risks for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data), including inherited and shared security risks, are transparently and mutually communicated with stakeholders.

title: System exposure minimisation
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Information about the design, configuration and operation of systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) is not publicly disclosed or shared externally unless necessary for commercial, legal, regulatory or security purposes, with any disclosure minimised, controlled and logged.

title: Supplier cyber security assurance
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are delivered and supported by trustworthy suppliers whose cyber security practices are regularly independently verified or otherwise risk-assessed.

title: Personnel suitability assurance
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Only personnel whose suitability and trustworthiness have been established, and are subject to ongoing assurance, are granted access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data).

title: Cyber security and safety
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Controls for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) do not compromise human, physical or environmental safety.

title: Legacy system management
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) that are not capable of meeting cyber security requirements are managed using compensating controls, along with enhanced monitoring and assurance activities, to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until they can be decommissioned or replaced.

title: Continuous cyber security improvement
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Govern cyber security principles
text: Security risk management and associated cyber security activities are continually measured and reviewed using cyber threat intelligence and assurance activities, including exercises informed by real-world cyber threats, to identify, prioritise and incorporate improvements in governance arrangements, shared responsibilities and the effectiveness of controls.

title: Asset identification
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Identify cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data) are continually and centrally identified and documented.

title: Asset interdependencies
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Identify cyber security principles
text: Interdependencies between systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are continually and centrally identified and documented, including how the compromise of one system could affect the security or business operations of other dependent systems.

title: Business criticality rating identification
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Identify cyber security principles
text: Business criticality ratings for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified and documented.

title: Security requirement identification
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Identify cyber security principles
text: Security requirements for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified and documented.

title: Resilience requirement identification
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Identify cyber security principles
text: Resilience requirements for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified and documented.

title: Security risk identification
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Identify cyber security principles
text: Security risks for an organisation and their systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified, including by using current strategic and sector-specific cyber threat intelligence and threat modelling, and are documented along with any associated risk management decisions.

title: Secure system lifecycle
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are planned, designed, developed, tested, deployed, maintained and decommissioned according to their business criticality ratings and security and resilience requirements using Secure by Design and Secure by Default principles and practices.

title: Cyber supply chain security
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Cyber supply chains supporting systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are secure, resilient and support effective and coordinated cyber security incident response.

title: Identity, credential and access management
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Robust and secure identity, credential and access management is used to establish, maintain and control access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) and to support effective detection of identity and credential misuse.

title: Least privilege access
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Personnel and services are granted the minimum access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) required to undertake their duties.

title: Secure administration
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are administered in a secure, accountable and auditable manner.

title: Secure configuration management
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are securely configured to approved and maintained baselines, including by reducing attack surfaces and attack paths, with configurations continually monitored and consistently enforced.

title: Vulnerability management
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Vulnerabilities in systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified, documented, validated and prioritised for remediation or mitigation in a timely manner, with all remediation and mitigation actions verified for effectiveness.

title: Trustworthy software
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Systems (operating systems and applications) only permit the execution of software that is supported, verified and authorised.

title: Cryptographic protection
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Data is encrypted and authenticated at rest and in transit using ASD-approved cryptography to protect its confidentiality and integrity.

title: Cryptographic agility
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are designed, configured and managed to support timely, prioritised and orderly changes to cryptography, including post-quantum cryptography.

title: Regular and proven backups
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are regularly backed up in a secure and proven manner, including through the validation of restoration capabilities.

title: Network segmentation and segregation
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are segmented into network zones based on business criticality and trust levels, with only authorised, controlled and monitored inbound and outbound communication paths between network zones permitted.

title: Operational technology isolation
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Operational technology systems (infrastructure) are logically and physically isolated from information technology systems (infrastructure) and all external infrastructure, with only authorised, controlled and monitored communication paths between systems permitted.

title: Remote access to operational technology
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Access to operational technology systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) over untrusted infrastructure is authorised, controlled and monitored.

title: Content filtering
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Data communicated between different security domains for systems (infrastructure and applications) is controlled and subject to inspection and verification.

title: Cyber security awareness training
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Personnel are provided with ongoing cyber security awareness training, including operational security considerations, tailored to their duties, access levels and current cyber threats.

title: Physical access control
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Protect cyber security principles
text: Physical access to facilities and systems (infrastructure and data) is restricted to authorised personnel and monitored for unusual activities.

title: Centralised event logging
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Detect cyber security principles
text: Security-relevant event logs and configuration changes for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are centrally collected, protected against unauthorised modification or deletion, and retained to support effective cyber security event detection and investigation.

title: Baselined high-risk access activities
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Detect cyber security principles
text: Baseline patterns of identity and credential access activities, privileged access activities, and remote access activities are established and maintained for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) to enable the detection of anomalous or unexpected behaviour.

title: Cyber security event detection
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Detect cyber security principles
text: Anomalous or unexpected events and behaviours for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

title: Cyber security incident identification
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Detect cyber security principles
text: Cyber security events are analysed in a timely manner to identify cyber security incidents.

title: Detection capability efficacy
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Detect cyber security principles
text: Cyber security event detection capabilities are regularly evaluated for effectiveness and continuously refined, including by using current strategic and sector-specific cyber threat intelligence, to improve the detection of cyber security events.

title: Cyber security incident planning
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Respond cyber security principles
text: Cyber security incident response, business continuity and disaster recovery plans for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) support continued business operations during cyber security incidents, and the resumption of normal business operations following cyber security incidents.

title: Cyber security incident coordination
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Respond cyber security principles
text: Cyber security incident roles and responsibilities are defined, documented and exercised to support the internal and external coordination and management of cyber security incidents, including responsibilities for declaring cyber security incidents and undertaking pre-approved response and recovery activities.

title: Cyber security incident response
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Respond cyber security principles
text: Cyber security incidents are contained, eradicated and recovered from in a timely manner.

title: Cyber security incident reporting
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Respond cyber security principles
text: Cyber security incidents, including associated response and recovery activities, are reported internally and externally to relevant bodies and stakeholders in a timely manner.

title: Cyber security incident insights
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Respond cyber security principles
text: Lessons learnt from cyber security incidents are captured, and areas for improvement are identified, prioritised and actioned in a timely manner.

title: System recovery assurance
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Recover cyber security principles
text: Following cyber security incidents, systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are verified through assurance activities to ensure they are secure and capable of supporting the resumption of normal business operations.

title: Business operations resumption
section: Cyber security principles / The cyber security principles / Recover cyber security principles
text: Residual security risks for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data), including inherited and shared security risks, are accepted prior to the resumption of normal business operations following cyber security incidents.

title: Control: ism-1997
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Embedding cyber security
text: The board of directors or executive committee defines clear roles and responsibilities for cyber security both within the board of directors or executive committee and broadly within their organisation.

title: Control: ism-1998
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Embedding cyber security
text: The board of directors or executive committee ensures that cyber security is integrated throughout all business functions within their organisation.

title: Control: ism-1999
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Embedding cyber security
text: The board of directors or executive committee ensures the cyber security strategy for their organisation is aligned with the overarching strategic direction and business strategy for their organisation.

title: Control: ism-2000
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Embedding cyber security
text: The board of directors or executive committee seeks regular briefings or reporting on the cyber security posture of their organisation, as well as the threat environment in which they operate, from internal and external subject matter experts.

title: Control: ism-2001
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Championing a positive cyber security culture
text: The board of directors or executive committee champions a positive cyber security culture within their organisation, including through leading by example.

title: Control: ism-2002
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Building cyber security expertise
text: The board of directors or executive committee maintains a sufficient level of cyber security literacy to fulfil both their fiduciary duties and any legislative or regulatory obligations.

title: Control: ism-2003
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Building cyber security expertise
text: The board of directors or executive committee maintains awareness of key cyber security recruitment activities, retention rates for cyber security personnel, and cyber security skills and experience gaps within their organisation.

title: Control: ism-2004
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Building cyber security expertise
text: The board of directors or executive committee supports the development of cyber security skills and experience for all personnel via internal and external cyber security awareness raising and training opportunities.

title: Control: ism-2005
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Identifying critical business assets
text: The board of directors or executive committee understands the business criticality of their organisation’s systems, including at least a basic understanding of what systems exist, their value, where they reside, who has access, who might seek access, how they are protected, and how that protection is verified.

title: Control: ism-2006
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Board of directors and executive committee / Planning for major cyber security incidents
text: The board of directors or executive committee plans for major cyber security incidents, including by participating in exercises, and understands their duties in relation to such cyber security incidents.

title: Control: ism-0714
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Providing cyber security leadership and guidance
text: A CISO is appointed to provide cyber security leadership and guidance for their organisation (covering IT and OT).

title: Control: ism-1478
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing the cyber security program
text: The CISO oversees their organisation’s cyber security program and ensures their organisation’s compliance with cyber security policy, standards, regulations and legislation.

title: Control: ism-1617
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing the cyber security program
text: The CISO regularly reviews and updates their organisation’s cyber security program to ensure its relevance in addressing cyber threats and harnessing business and cyber security opportunities.

title: Control: ism-1966
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing the cyber security program
text: The CISO develops, implements, maintains and regularly verifies a register of systems used by their organisation.

title: Control: ism-0724
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing the cyber security program
text: The CISO implements cyber security measurement metrics and key performance indicators for their organisation.

title: Control: ism-0725
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Coordinating cyber security
text: The CISO coordinates cyber security and business alignment through a cyber security steering committee or advisory board, comprising key cyber security and business executives, which meets formally and regularly.

title: Control: ism-0726
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Coordinating cyber security
text: The CISO coordinates security risk management activities between cyber security and business teams.

title: Control: ism-0718
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Reporting on cyber security
text: The CISO regularly reports directly to their organisation’s board of directors or executive committee on cyber security matters.

title: Control: ism-1918
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Reporting on cyber security
text: The CISO regularly reports directly to their organisation’s audit, risk and compliance committee (or equivalent) on cyber security matters.

title: Control: ism-0733
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing cyber security incident response activities
text: The CISO is fully aware of all cyber security incidents within their organisation.

title: Control: ism-1618
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing cyber security incident response activities
text: The CISO oversees their organisation’s response to cyber security incidents.

title: Control: ism-0734
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Contributing to business continuity and disaster recovery planning
text: The CISO contributes to the development, implementation and maintenance of business continuity and disaster recovery plans for their organisation to ensure that business-critical services are supported appropriately in the event of a disaster.

title: Control: ism-0720
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Communicating a cyber security vision and strategy
text: The CISO oversees the development, implementation and maintenance of a cyber security communications strategy to assist in communicating the cyber security vision and strategy for their organisation.

title: Control: ism-0731
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Working with suppliers
text: The CISO oversees cyber supply chain risk management activities for their organisation.

title: Control: ism-0732
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Receiving and managing a dedicated cyber security budget
text: The CISO receives and manages a dedicated cyber security budget for their organisation.

title: Control: ism-0717
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing cyber security personnel
text: The CISO oversees the management of cyber security personnel within their organisation.

title: Control: ism-2020
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing cyber security personnel
text: The CISO ensures sufficient cyber security personnel, with the right skills and experience, are acquired to support cyber security activities within their organisation.

title: Control: ism-0735
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / Chief information security officer / Overseeing cyber security awareness training
text: The CISO oversees the development, implementation and maintenance of their organisation’s cyber security awareness training program.

title: Control: ism-1071
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / System ownership and oversight
text: Each system has a designated system owner.

title: Control: ism-1525
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / System ownership and oversight
text: System owners register each system with its authorising officer.

title: Control: ism-1633
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, determine the system boundary, business criticality, and security and resilience objectives for each system based on an assessment of the impact if it were to be compromised or attacked.

title: Control: ism-1203
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, conduct a threat and risk assessment for each system.

title: Control: ism-1634
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, select controls for each system and tailor them to achieve desired security and resilience objectives.

title: Control: ism-0009
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, identify any supplementary controls required based upon the unique nature of each system, its operating environment and the organisation’s risk tolerances.

title: Control: ism-1635
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners implement controls for each system and its operating environment.

title: Control: ism-1636
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, ensure controls for each non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET system and its operating environment undergo a security assessment by their organisation’s own assessors or Infosec Registered Assessor Program (IRAP) assessors to determine if they have been implemented correctly and are operating as intended.

title: Control: ism-1967
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, ensure controls for each TOP SECRET system and its operating environment, including each sensitive compartmented information system and its operating environment, undergo a security assessment by ASD assessors (or their delegates) to determine if they have been implemented correctly and are operating as intended.

title: Control: ism-0027
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners obtain an authorisation to operate for each non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET system from its authorising officer.

title: Control: ism-1968
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners obtain an authorisation to operate for each TOP SECRET system, including for each sensitive compartmented information system, from Director-General ASD (or their delegate).

title: Control: ism-1526
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners continuously monitor the security of each system, and manage associated cyber threats, security risks and controls.

title: Control: ism-2021
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Protecting systems and their resources
text: System owners implement and maintain data minimisation practices for each of their systems.

title: Control: ism-1587
section: Guidelines for cyber security roles / System owners / Annual reporting of system security status
text: System owners report the security status of each system to its authorising officer at least annually.

title: Control: ism-0576
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Cyber security incident management policy
text: A cyber security incident management policy, and associated cyber security incident response plan, is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1784
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Cyber security incident management policy
text: The cyber security incident management policy, including the associated cyber security incident response plan, is exercised at least annually.

title: Control: ism-0125
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Cyber security incident register
text: A cyber security incident register is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1803
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Cyber security incident register
text:
A cyber security incident register contains the following for each cyber security incident:

- the date the cyber security incident occurred
- the date the cyber security incident was discovered
- a description of the cyber security incident
- any actions taken in response to the cyber security incident
- to whom the cyber security incident was reported.

title: Control: ism-1625
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Insider threat mitigation program
text: An insider threat mitigation program is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1626
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Insider threat mitigation program
text: Legal advice is sought regarding the development and implementation of an insider threat mitigation program.

title: Control: ism-0123
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Reporting cyber security incidents
text: Cyber security incidents are reported to the chief information security officer, or one of their delegates, as soon as possible after they occur or are discovered.

title: Control: ism-0140
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Reporting cyber security incidents to ASD
text: Cyber security incidents are reported to ASD as soon as possible after they occur or are discovered.

title: Control: ism-1880
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Reporting cyber security incidents to customers and the public
text: Cyber security incidents that involve customer data are reported to customers and the public in a timely manner after they occur or are discovered.

title: Control: ism-1881
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Managing cyber security incidents / Reporting cyber security incidents to customers and the public
text: Cyber security incidents that do not involve customer data are reported to customers and the public in a timely manner after they occur or are discovered.

title: Control: ism-1819
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Enacting cyber security incident response plans
text: Following the identification of a cyber security incident, the cyber security incident response plan is enacted.

title: Control: ism-0133
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing data spills
text: When a data spill occurs, data owners are advised and access to the data is restricted.

title: Control: ism-0917
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing malicious code infections
text:
When malicious code is detected, the following steps are taken to handle the infection:

- the infected systems are isolated
- all previously connected media used in the period leading up to the infection are scanned for signs of infection and isolated if necessary
- antivirus applications are used to remove the infection from infected systems and media
- if the infection cannot be reliably removed, systems are restored from a known good backup or rebuilt.

title: Control: ism-1969
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing malicious code infections
text: Malicious code, when stored or communicated, is treated beforehand to prevent accidental execution.

title: Control: ism-1970
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing malicious code infections
text: Malicious code processing for cyber security incident response or research purposes is conducted in a dedicated analysis environment segregated from other systems.

title: Control: ism-0137
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing intrusions
text: Legal advice is sought before allowing intrusion activity to continue on a system for the purpose of collecting further data or evidence.

title: Control: ism-1609
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing intrusions
text: System owners are consulted before allowing intrusion activity to continue on a system for the purpose of collecting further data or evidence.

title: Control: ism-1731
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing intrusions
text: Planning and coordination of intrusion remediation activities are conducted on a separate system to that which has been compromised.

title: Control: ism-1732
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing intrusions
text: To the extent possible, all intrusion remediation activities are conducted in a coordinated manner during the same planned outage.

title: Control: ism-1213
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Handling and containing intrusions
text: Following intrusion remediation activities, full network traffic is captured for at least seven days and analysed to determine whether malicious actors have been successfully removed from the system.

title: Control: ism-0138
section: Guidelines for cyber security incidents / Responding to cyber security incidents / Maintaining the integrity of evidence
text:
The integrity of evidence gathered during an investigation is maintained by investigators:

- recording all their actions
- maintaining a proper chain of custody
- following all instructions provided by relevant law enforcement agencies.

title: Control: ism-1631
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Cyber supply chain risk management activities
text: Suppliers of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services associated with systems are identified.

title: Control: ism-1452
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Cyber supply chain risk management activities
text: A supply chain risk assessment is performed for suppliers of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services to assess the impact to a system’s security risk profile.

title: Control: ism-1567
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Cyber supply chain risk management activities
text: Suppliers identified as high risk by a cyber supply chain risk assessment are not used.

title: Control: ism-1568
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Cyber supply chain risk management activities
text: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are procured from suppliers that have demonstrated a commitment to the security of their products and services.

title: Control: ism-1882
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Cyber supply chain risk management activities
text: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are procured from suppliers that have demonstrated a commitment to transparency for their products and services.

title: Control: ism-1632
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Cyber supply chain risk management activities
text: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are procured from suppliers that have a strong track record of maintaining the security of their own systems.

title: Control: ism-1569
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Cyber supply chain risk management activities
text: A shared responsibility model is created, documented and shared between suppliers and their customers to articulate the security responsibilities of each party.

title: Control: ism-1785
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Supplier relationship management
text: A supplier relationship management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1786
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Supplier relationship management
text: An approved supplier list is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1787
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Sourcing operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services
text: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are sourced from approved suppliers.

title: Control: ism-1788
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Sourcing operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services
text: Multiple potential suppliers are identified for sourcing critical operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services.

title: Control: ism-1789
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Sourcing operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services
text: Sufficient spares of critical IT equipment and OT equipment are sourced and kept in reserve.

title: Control: ism-1790
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Delivery of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services
text: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are delivered in a manner that maintains their integrity.

title: Control: ism-1791
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Delivery of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services
text: The integrity of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are assessed as part of acceptance of products and services.

title: Control: ism-1792
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Cyber supply chain risk management / Delivery of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services
text: The authenticity of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are assessed as part of acceptance of products and services.

title: Control: ism-1736
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Managed services
text: A managed service register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-1737
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Managed services
text:
A managed service register contains the following for each managed service:

- managed service provider’s name
- managed service’s name
- purpose for using the managed service
- sensitivity or classification of data involved
- due date for the next security assessment of the managed service
- contractual arrangements for the managed service
- point of contact for users of the managed service
- 24/7 contact details for the managed service provider.

title: Control: ism-1793
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Assessment of managed service providers
text: Managed service providers and their non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET managed services undergo an Infosec Registered Assessor Program (IRAP) assessment, using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the IRAP assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

title: Control: ism-1971
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Assessment of managed service providers
text: Managed service providers and their TOP SECRET managed services, including sensitive compartmented information managed services, undergo a security assessment by ASD assessors (or their delegates), using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the security assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

title: Control: ism-1637
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Outsourced cloud services
text: An outsourced cloud service register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-1638
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Outsourced cloud services
text:
An outsourced cloud service register contains the following for each outsourced cloud service:

- cloud service provider’s name
- cloud service’s name
- purpose for using the cloud service
- sensitivity or classification of data involved
- due date for the next security assessment of the cloud service
- contractual arrangements for the cloud service
- point of contact for users of the cloud service
- 24/7 contact details for the cloud service provider.

title: Control: ism-1529
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Outsourced cloud services
text: Only community or private clouds are used for outsourced SECRET and TOP SECRET cloud services.

title: Control: ism-1570
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Assessment of outsourced cloud service providers
text: Outsourced cloud service providers and their non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET cloud services undergo an IRAP assessment, using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the IRAP assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

title: Control: ism-1972
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Assessment of outsourced cloud service providers
text: Outsourced cloud service providers and their TOP SECRET cloud services, including sensitive compartmented information cloud services, undergo a security assessment by ASD assessors (or their delegates), using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the security assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

title: Control: ism-1395
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: Service providers, including any subcontractors, provide an appropriate level of protection for any data entrusted to them or their services.

title: Control: ism-0072
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: Security requirements associated with the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data are documented in contractual arrangements with service providers and regularly reviewed to ensure they remain fit for purpose.

title: Control: ism-1571
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: The right to verify compliance with security requirements is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-1738
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: The right to verify compliance with security requirements documented in contractual arrangements with service providers is regularly exercised.

title: Control: ism-1804
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: Break clauses associated with failure to meet security requirements are documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-0141
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: The requirement for service providers to report cyber security incidents to a designated point of contact as soon as possible after they occur or are discovered is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-1794
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: A minimum notification period of one month by service providers for significant changes to their own service provider arrangements is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-1451
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: Types of data and its ownership is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-1572
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: The regions or availability zones where data will be processed, stored and communicated, as well as a minimum notification period for any configuration changes, is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-1573
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: Access to all logs relating to an organisation’s data and services is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-1574
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: The storage of data in a portable manner that enables backups, service migration and service decommissioning without any loss of data is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-1575
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Contractual security requirements with service providers
text: A minimum notification period of one month for the cessation of any services by a service provider is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

title: Control: ism-1073
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Access to systems by service providers
text: An organisation’s systems are not accessed or administered by a service provider unless a contractual arrangement exists between the organisation and the service provider to do so.

title: Control: ism-1576
section: Guidelines for procurement and outsourcing / Managed services and cloud services / Access to systems by service providers
text: If an organisation’s systems are accessed or administered by a service provider in an unauthorised manner, the organisation is immediately notified.

title: Control: ism-0039
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / Development and maintenance of cyber security documentation / Cyber security strategy
text: A cyber security strategy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0047
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / Development and maintenance of cyber security documentation / Approval of cyber security documentation
text: Organisational-level cyber security documentation is approved by the chief information security officer while system-specific cyber security documentation is approved by the system’s authorising officer.

title: Control: ism-1739
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / Development and maintenance of cyber security documentation / Approval of cyber security documentation
text: A system’s security architecture is approved prior to the development of the system.

title: Control: ism-0888
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / Development and maintenance of cyber security documentation / Maintenance of cyber security documentation
text: Cyber security documentation is reviewed at least annually and includes a ‘current as at \[date\]’ or equivalent statement.

title: Control: ism-1602
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / Development and maintenance of cyber security documentation / Communication of cyber security documentation
text: Cyber security documentation, including notification of subsequent changes, is communicated to all stakeholders.

title: Control: ism-0041
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / System-specific cyber security documentation / System security plan
text: Systems have a system security plan that includes an overview of the system (covering the system’s purpose, the system boundary and how the system is managed) as well as an annex that covers applicable controls from this document and any additional controls that have been identified and implemented.

title: Control: ism-0043
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / System-specific cyber security documentation / Cyber security incident response plan
text:
Systems have a cyber security incident response plan that covers the following:

- guidelines on what constitutes a cyber security incident
- the types of cyber security incidents likely to be encountered and the expected response to each type
- how to report cyber security incidents, internally to an organisation and externally to relevant authorities
- other parties that need to be informed in the event of a cyber security incident
- the authority, or authorities, responsible for investigating and responding to cyber security incidents
- the criteria by which an investigation of a cyber security incident would be requested from a law enforcement agency, the Australian Signals Directorate or other relevant authority
- the steps necessary to ensure the integrity of evidence relating to a cyber security incident
- system contingency measures or a reference to such details if they are in a separate document.

title: Control: ism-0912
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / System-specific cyber security documentation / Change and configuration management plan
text:
Systems have a change and configuration management plan that includes:

- the establishment and maintenance of authorised baseline configurations for systems
- what constitutes routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems
- how changes to the configuration of systems will be requested, tracked and documented
- who needs to be consulted prior to routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems
- who needs to approve routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems
- who needs to be notified of routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems
- what additional change management and configuration management processes and procedures need to be followed before, during and after routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems.

title: Control: ism-1163
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / System-specific cyber security documentation / Continuous monitoring plan
text:
Systems have a continuous monitoring plan that includes:

- conducting security assessment activities to identify vulnerabilities
- analysing identified vulnerabilities to determine their potential impact
- implementing mitigations based on risk, effectiveness and cost.

title: Control: ism-1563
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / System-specific cyber security documentation / Security assessment report
text:
At the conclusion of a security assessment for a system, a security assessment report is produced by the assessor and covers:

- the scope of the security assessment
- the system’s strengths and weaknesses
- security risks associated with the operation of the system
- the effectiveness of the implementation of controls
- any recommended remediation actions.

title: Control: ism-1564
section: Guidelines for cyber security documentation / System-specific cyber security documentation / Plan of action and milestones
text: At the conclusion of a security assessment for a system, a plan of action and milestones is produced by the system owner.

title: Control: ism-1973
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to systems
text: Non-classified systems are secured in suitably secure facilities.

title: Control: ism-0810
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to systems
text: Classified systems are secured in facilities that meet the requirements for a security zone suitable for their classification.

title: Control: ism-1974
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment
text: Non-classified servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment are secured in suitably secure server rooms or communications rooms.

title: Control: ism-1053
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment
text: Classified servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment are secured in server rooms or communications rooms that meet the requirements for a security zone suitable for their classification.

title: Control: ism-1975
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment
text: Non-classified servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment are secured in suitably secure security containers.

title: Control: ism-1530
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment
text: Classified servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment are secured in security containers suitable for their classification taking into account the combination of security zones they reside in.

title: Control: ism-0813
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment
text: Server rooms, communications rooms and security containers are not left in unsecured states.

title: Control: ism-1074
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment
text: Keys or equivalent access mechanisms to server rooms, communications rooms and security containers are appropriately controlled.

title: Control: ism-1296
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Physical access to network devices in public areas
text: Physical security is implemented to protect network devices in public areas from physical damage or unauthorised access.

title: Control: ism-1543
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Bringing radio frequency and infrared devices into facilities
text: An authorised RF and IR device register for SECRET and TOP SECRET areas is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-0225
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Bringing radio frequency and infrared devices into facilities
text: Unauthorised RF and IR devices are not brought into SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

title: Control: ism-0829
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Bringing radio frequency and infrared devices into facilities
text: Security measures are used to detect and respond to unauthorised RF devices in SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

title: Control: ism-2069
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Bringing photographic and video recording devices into facilities
text: An authorised photographic and video recording device register for SECRET and TOP SECRET areas is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-2070
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Bringing photographic and video recording devices into facilities
text: Unauthorised photographic and video recording devices are not brought into SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

title: Control: ism-2007
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Bringing medical devices into facilities
text: An authorised medical device register for SECRET and TOP SECRET areas is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-2008
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Bringing medical devices into facilities
text:
Medical devices authorised to be brought into SECRET and TOP SECRET areas meet, at a minimum, the following criteria:

- are listed on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods
- have been prescribed by a legally qualified medical practitioner
- have been commercially purchased within Australia
- do not have inbuilt cellular connectivity
- can operate independently of mobile devices
- where possible, have Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and other forms of wireless connectivity disabled when operating within SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

title: Control: ism-2009
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Bringing medical devices into facilities
text: Unauthorised medical devices are not brought into SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

title: Control: ism-0164
section: Guidelines for physical security / Facilities and systems / Preventing observation by unauthorised people
text: Unauthorised people are prevented from observing systems, in particular workstation displays and keyboards, within facilities.

title: Control: ism-0161
section: Guidelines for physical security / IT equipment and media / Securing IT equipment and media
text: IT equipment and media are secured when not in use.

title: Control: ism-0252
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Providing cyber security awareness training
text:
Cyber security awareness training is undertaken annually by all personnel and covers:

- the purpose of the cyber security awareness training
- security appointments and contacts
- authorised use of systems and their resources
- protection of systems and their resources
- reporting of cyber security incidents and suspected compromises of systems and their resources.

title: Control: ism-1565
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Providing cyber security awareness training
text: Tailored privileged user training is undertaken annually by all privileged users.

title: Control: ism-2022
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Providing cyber security awareness training
text: A cyber security awareness training register is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1740
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Managing and reporting suspicious changes to banking details or payment requests
text: Personnel dealing with banking details and payment requests are advised of what business email compromise is and how to manage and report it.

title: Control: ism-2071
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Managing and reporting suspicious requests to disclose or change user account details
text: Personnel dealing with user account details are advised of what social engineering attacks are, how to manage such situations and how to report them.

title: Control: ism-0817
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Reporting suspicious contact via online services
text: Personnel are advised of what suspicious contact via online services is and how to report it.

title: Control: ism-0820
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Posting work-related information on online services
text: Personnel are advised not to post work-related information on unauthorised online services, and to report cases where such information is posted.

title: Control: ism-2104
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Posting work-related information on online services
text: Personnel are advised not to post information about their security clearance and briefings on unauthorised online services, and to report cases where such information is posted.

title: Control: ism-2105
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Posting work-related information on online services
text: Personnel are advised to limit posting information about their work-related duties on unauthorised online services, and to report cases where such information is posted.

title: Control: ism-2106
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Posting work-related information on online services
text: Personnel are advised to limit posting information about their work-related skills and experience on unauthorised online services, and to report cases where such information is posted.

title: Control: ism-0821
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Posting personal information on online services
text: Personnel are advised of security risks associated with posting personal information on online services.

title: Control: ism-1146
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Posting personal information on online services
text: Personnel are advised to maintain separate personal user accounts from any work user accounts they use for online services.

title: Control: ism-2107
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Posting personal information on online services
text: Personnel are encouraged to use any available privacy settings to restrict who can view personal information they post on online services.

title: Control: ism-0824
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Sending and receiving files via online services
text: Personnel are advised not to send or receive files via unauthorised online services.

title: Control: ism-1864
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / System usage policy
text: A system usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-2074
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / General-purpose artificial intelligence usage policy
text: A general-purpose AI usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0258
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Web usage policy
text: A web usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0432
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / System access requirements
text: Access requirements for systems and their resources are documented in their system security plan.

title: Control: ism-0434
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / System access requirements
text: Personnel undergo appropriate employment screening and, where necessary, hold an appropriate security clearance before being granted access to systems and their resources.

title: Control: ism-0435
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / System access requirements
text: Personnel receive any necessary briefings before being granted access to systems and their resources.

title: Control: ism-1865
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / System access requirements
text: Personnel agree to abide by system usage policies before being granted access to systems and their resources.

title: Control: ism-0414
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / User identification
text: Personnel granted access to systems and their resources are uniquely identifiable.

title: Control: ism-0415
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / User identification
text: The use of shared user accounts is strictly controlled, and personnel using such accounts are uniquely identifiable.

title: Control: ism-1583
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / User identification
text: Personnel who are contractors are identified as such.

title: Control: ism-0420
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / User identification
text: Where systems process, store or communicate AUSTEO, AGAO or REL data, personnel who are foreign nationals are identified as such, including by their specific nationality.

title: Control: ism-0405
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Unprivileged access to systems
text: Requests for unprivileged access to systems and their resources are validated when first requested.

title: Control: ism-1852
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Unprivileged access to systems
text: Unprivileged access to systems and their resources is limited to only what is required for users and services to undertake their duties.

title: Control: ism-1566
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Unprivileged access to systems
text: Use of unprivileged access is centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-0409
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Unprivileged access to systems by foreign nationals
text: Foreign nationals, including seconded foreign nationals, do not have access to systems that process, store or communicate AUSTEO or REL data unless effective controls are in place to ensure such data is not accessible to them.

title: Control: ism-0411
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Unprivileged access to systems by foreign nationals
text: Foreign nationals, excluding seconded foreign nationals, do not have access to systems that process, store or communicate AGAO data unless effective controls are in place to ensure such data is not accessible to them.

title: Control: ism-1507
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Requests for privileged access to systems and their resources are validated when first requested.

title: Control: ism-1508
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Privileged access to systems and their resources is limited to only what is required for users and services to undertake their duties.

title: Control: ism-1175
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Privileged user accounts (excluding those explicitly authorised to access online services) are prevented from accessing the internet, email and web services.

title: Control: ism-1883
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Privileged user accounts explicitly authorised to access online services are strictly limited to only what is required for users and services to undertake their duties.

title: Control: ism-1649
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Just-in-time administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources.

title: Control: ism-0445
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Privileged users are assigned a dedicated privileged user account to be used solely for duties requiring privileged access.

title: Control: ism-1263
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Unique privileged user accounts are used for administering individual server applications.

title: Control: ism-1509
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Privileged access events are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-1650
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems
text: Privileged user account and security group management events are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-0446
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems by foreign nationals
text: Foreign nationals, including seconded foreign nationals, do not have privileged access to systems that process, store or communicate AUSTEO or REL data.

title: Control: ism-0447
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Privileged access to systems by foreign nationals
text: Foreign nationals, excluding seconded foreign nationals, do not have privileged access to systems that process, store or communicate AGAO data.

title: Control: ism-0430
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Suspension of access to systems
text: Access to systems and their resources are removed or suspended the same day personnel no longer have a legitimate requirement for access.

title: Control: ism-1591
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Suspension of access to systems
text: Access to systems and their resources are removed or suspended as soon as practicable when personnel are detected undertaking malicious activities.

title: Control: ism-1404
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Suspension of access to systems
text: Unprivileged access to systems and their resources are disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

title: Control: ism-1648
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Suspension of access to systems
text: Privileged access to systems and their resources are disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

title: Control: ism-1647
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Suspension of access to systems
text: Privileged access to systems and their resources are disabled after 12 months unless revalidated.

title: Control: ism-0407
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Recording authorisation for personnel to access systems
text:
A secure record is maintained for the life of systems and their resources that covers the following for each user:

- their user identification
- their signed agreement to abide by system usage policies
- who authorised their access
- when their access was granted
- the level of access they were granted
- when their access, and their level of access, was last reviewed
- when their level of access was changed, and to what extent (if applicable)
- when their access was withdrawn (if applicable).

title: Control: ism-0441
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Temporary access to systems
text: When personnel are granted temporary access to systems and their resources, effective controls are put in place to restrict their access to only data required for them to undertake their duties.

title: Control: ism-0443
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Temporary access to systems
text: Temporary access is not granted to systems that process, store or communicate caveated or sensitive compartmented information.

title: Control: ism-1610
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Emergency access to systems
text: A method of emergency access to systems and their resources is documented and tested at least once when initially implemented and each time fundamental information technology infrastructure changes occur.

title: Control: ism-1611
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Emergency access to systems
text: Break glass accounts are only used when normal authentication processes cannot be used.

title: Control: ism-1612
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Emergency access to systems
text: Break glass accounts are only used for specific authorised activities.

title: Control: ism-1614
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Emergency access to systems
text: Break glass account credentials are changed by the account custodian after they are accessed by any other party.

title: Control: ism-1615
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Emergency access to systems
text: Break glass accounts are tested after credentials are changed.

title: Control: ism-1613
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Emergency access to systems
text: Use of break glass accounts is centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-0078
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Control of Australian systems
text: Systems processing, storing or communicating AUSTEO or AGAO data remain at all times under the control of an Australian national working for or on behalf of the Australian Government.

title: Control: ism-0854
section: Guidelines for personnel security / Access to systems and their resources / Control of Australian systems
text: AUSTEO and AGAO data can only be accessed from systems under the sole control of the Australian Government that are located within facilities authorised by the Australian Government.

title: Control: ism-0181
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure standards
text: Cabling infrastructure is installed in accordance with relevant Australian Standards, as directed by the Australian Communications and Media Authority.

title: Control: ism-1111
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Use of fibre-optic cables
text: Fibre-optic cables are used for cabling infrastructure instead of copper cables.

title: Control: ism-0211
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable register
text: A cable register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-0208
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable register
text:
A cable register contains the following for each cable:

- cable identifier
- cable colour
- sensitivity/classification
- source
- destination
- location
- seal numbers (if applicable).

title: Control: ism-1645
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Floor plan diagrams
text: Floor plan diagrams are developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-1646
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Floor plan diagrams
text:
Floor plan diagrams contain the following:

- cable paths (including ingress and egress points between floors)
- cable reticulation system and conduit paths
