section: Guidelines for personnel security / Cyber security awareness training / Sending and receiving files via online services
text: Personnel are advised not to send or receive files via unauthorised online services.

title: Control: ism-0181
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure standards
text: Cabling infrastructure is installed in accordance with relevant Australian Standards, as directed by the Australian Communications and Media Authority.

title: Control: ism-1111
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Use of fibre-optic cables
text: Fibre-optic cables are used for cabling infrastructure instead of copper cables.

title: Control: ism-0211
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable register
text: A cable register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-0208
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable register
text:
A cable register contains the following for each cable:

- cable identifier
- cable colour
- sensitivity/classification
- source
- destination
- location
- seal numbers (if applicable).

title: Control: ism-1645
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Floor plan diagrams
text: Floor plan diagrams are developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-1646
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Floor plan diagrams
text:
Floor plan diagrams contain the following:

- cable paths (including ingress and egress points between floors)
- cable reticulation system and conduit paths
- floor concentration boxes
- wall outlet boxes
- network cabinets.

title: Control: ism-0206
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable labelling processes and procedures
text: Cable labelling processes, and supporting cable labelling procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1096
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Labelling cables
text: Cables are labelled at each end with sufficient source and destination details to enable the physical identification and inspection of the cable.

title: Control: ism-1639
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Labelling building management cables
text: Building management cables are labelled with their purpose in black writing on a yellow background, with a minimum size of 2.5 cm x 1 cm, and attached at five-metre intervals.

title: Control: ism-1640
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Labelling cables for foreign systems in Australian facilities
text: Cables for foreign systems installed in Australian facilities are labelled at inspection points.

title: Control: ism-1820
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable colours
text: Cables for individual systems use a consistent colour.

title: Control: ism-0926
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable colours
text: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED cables are coloured neither salmon pink nor red.

title: Control: ism-1718
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable colours
text: SECRET cables are coloured salmon pink.

title: Control: ism-1719
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable colours
text: TOP SECRET cables are coloured red.

title: Control: ism-1216
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable colour non-conformance
text: SECRET and TOP SECRET cables with non-conformant cable colouring are banded with the appropriate colour and labelled at inspection points.

title: Control: ism-1112
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable inspectability
text: Cables in non-TOP SECRET areas are inspectable every five metres or less.

title: Control: ism-1119
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cable inspectability
text: Cables in TOP SECRET areas are fully inspectable for their entire length.

title: Control: ism-0187
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Common cable bundles and conduits
text: SECRET cables, when bundled together or run in conduit, are run exclusively in their own individual cable bundle or conduit.

title: Control: ism-1821
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Common cable bundles and conduits
text: TOP SECRET cables, when bundled together or run in conduit, are run exclusively in their own individual cable bundle or conduit.

title: Control: ism-1114
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Common cable reticulation systems
text: Cable bundles or conduits sharing a common cable reticulation system have a dividing partition or visible gap between each cable bundle and conduit.

title: Control: ism-1130
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Enclosed cable reticulation systems
text: In shared facilities, cables are run in an enclosed cable reticulation system.

title: Control: ism-1164
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Covers for enclosed cable reticulation systems
text: In shared facilities, conduits or the front covers of ducts, cable trays in floors and ceilings, and associated fittings are clear plastic.

title: Control: ism-0195
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Sealing cable reticulation systems and conduits
text: In shared facilities, uniquely identifiable SCEC-approved tamper-evident seals are used to seal all removable covers on TOP SECRET cable reticulation systems.

title: Control: ism-0194
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Sealing cable reticulation systems and conduits
text: In shared facilities, a visible smear of conduit glue is used to seal all plastic conduit joints and TOP SECRET conduits connected by threaded lock nuts.

title: Control: ism-0201
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Labelling conduits
text: Labels for TOP SECRET conduits are a minimum size of 2.5 cm x 1 cm, attached at five-metre intervals and marked as ‘TS RUN’.

title: Control: ism-1115
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cables in walls
text: Cables from cable trays to wall outlet boxes are run in flexible or plastic conduit.

title: Control: ism-1133
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Cables in party walls
text: In shared facilities, TOP SECRET cables are not run in party walls.

title: Control: ism-1122
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Wall penetrations
text: Where wall penetrations exit a TOP SECRET area into a lower classified area, TOP SECRET cables are encased in conduit with all gaps between the TOP SECRET conduit and the wall filled with an appropriate sealing compound.

title: Control: ism-1105
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Wall outlet boxes
text: SECRET and TOP SECRET wall outlet boxes contain exclusively SECRET or TOP SECRET cables.

title: Control: ism-1095
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Labelling wall outlet boxes
text: Wall outlet boxes denote the systems, cable identifiers and wall outlet box identifier.

title: Control: ism-1822
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Wall outlet box colours
text: Wall outlet boxes for individual systems use a consistent colour.

title: Control: ism-1107
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Wall outlet box colours
text: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED wall outlet boxes are coloured neither salmon pink nor red.

title: Control: ism-1720
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Wall outlet box colours
text: SECRET wall outlet boxes are coloured salmon pink.

title: Control: ism-1721
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Wall outlet box colours
text: TOP SECRET wall outlet boxes are coloured red.

title: Control: ism-1109
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Wall outlet box covers
text: Wall outlet box covers are clear plastic.

title: Control: ism-0218
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Fly lead installation
text: If TOP SECRET fibre-optic fly leads exceeding five metres in length are used to connect wall outlet boxes to IT equipment, they are run in a protective and easily inspected pathway that is clearly labelled at the IT equipment end with the wall outlet box’s identifier.

title: Control: ism-1102
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Connecting cable reticulation systems to cabinets
text: Cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets are terminated as close as possible to the cabinet.

title: Control: ism-1101
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Connecting cable reticulation systems to cabinets
text: In TOP SECRET areas, cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets in server rooms or communications rooms are terminated as close as possible to the cabinet.

title: Control: ism-1103
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Connecting cable reticulation systems to cabinets
text: In TOP SECRET areas, cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets not in server rooms or communications rooms are terminated at the boundary of the cabinet.

title: Control: ism-1098
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Terminating cables in cabinets
text: SECRET cables are terminated in an individual cabinet; or for small systems, a cabinet with a division plate between any SECRET cables and non-SECRET cables.

title: Control: ism-1100
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Terminating cables in cabinets
text: TOP SECRET cables are terminated in an individual TOP SECRET cabinet.

title: Control: ism-0213
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Terminating cables on patch panels
text: SECRET and TOP SECRET cables are terminated on their own individual patch panels.

title: Control: ism-0216
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Physical separation of cabinets and patch panels
text: TOP SECRET patch panels are installed in individual TOP SECRET cabinets.

title: Control: ism-0217
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Physical separation of cabinets and patch panels
text:
Where spatial constraints demand non-TOP SECRET patch panels be installed in the same cabinet as a TOP SECRET patch panel:

- a physical barrier in the cabinet is provided to separate patch panels
- only personnel holding a Positive Vetting security clearance have access to the cabinet
- approval from the TOP SECRET system’s authorising officer is obtained prior to installation.

title: Control: ism-1116
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Physical separation of cabinets and patch panels
text: A visible gap exists between TOP SECRET cabinets and non-TOP SECRET cabinets.

title: Control: ism-0198
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Audio secure rooms
text: When penetrating a TOP SECRET audio secure room, the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation is consulted and all directions provided are complied with.

title: Control: ism-1123
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Cabling infrastructure / Power reticulation
text: A power distribution board with a feed from an Uninterruptible Power Supply is used to power all TOP SECRET IT equipment.

title: Control: ism-0250
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Emanation security / Electromagnetic interference/electromagnetic compatibility standards
text: IT equipment meets industry and government standards relating to electromagnetic interference/electromagnetic compatibility.

title: Control: ism-1884
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Emanation security / Emanation security doctrine
text: Emanation security doctrine produced by ASD for the management of emanation security matters is complied with.

title: Control: ism-1137
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Emanation security / Emanation security risk assessments
text: System owners deploying SECRET or TOP SECRET systems within fixed facilities contact ASD for an emanation security risk assessment.

title: Control: ism-0249
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Emanation security / Emanation security risk assessments
text: System owners deploying SECRET or TOP SECRET systems in mobile platforms, or as a deployable capability, contact ASD for an emanation security risk assessment.

title: Control: ism-0246
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Emanation security / Emanation security risk assessments
text: When an emanation security risk assessment is required, it is sought as early as possible in a system’s life cycle.

title: Control: ism-1885
section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure / Emanation security / Emanation security risk assessments
text: Recommended actions contained within emanation security mitigation advice issued for systems are implemented by system owners.

title: Control: ism-1078
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Telephone system usage policy
text: A telephone system usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0229
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Personnel awareness
text: Personnel are advised of the permitted sensitivity or classification of information that can be discussed over internal and external telephone systems.

title: Control: ism-0230
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Personnel awareness
text: Personnel are advised of security risks posed by non-secure telephone systems in areas where sensitive or classified conversations can occur.

title: Control: ism-0231
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Personnel awareness
text: When using cryptographic equipment to permit different levels of conversation for different kinds of connections, telephone systems give a visual indication of what kind of connection has been made.

title: Control: ism-0232
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Protecting conversations
text: Telephone systems used for sensitive or classified conversations encrypt all traffic that passes over external systems.

title: Control: ism-0233
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Cordless telephone systems
text: Cordless telephone handsets and headsets are not used for sensitive or classified conversations unless all communications are encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.

title: Control: ism-0235
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Speakerphones
text: Speakerphones are not used on telephone systems in TOP SECRET areas unless the telephone system is located in an audio secure room, the room is audio secure during conversations and only personnel involved in conversations are present in the room.

title: Control: ism-0236
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Off-hook audio protection
text: Off-hook audio protection features are used on telephone systems in areas where background conversations may exceed the sensitivity or classification that the telephone system is authorised for communicating.

title: Control: ism-0931
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Telephone systems / Off-hook audio protection
text: In SECRET and TOP SECRET areas, push-to-talk handsets or push-to-talk headsets are used to meet any off-hook audio protection requirements.

title: Control: ism-1562
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony infrastructure hardening
text: Video conferencing and IP telephony infrastructure is hardened.

title: Control: ism-0546
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Video-aware and voice-aware firewalls and proxies
text: When video conferencing or IP telephony traffic passes through a gateway containing a firewall or proxy, a video-aware or voice-aware firewall or proxy is used.

title: Control: ism-0548
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Protecting video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony traffic
text: Video conferencing and IP telephony calls are established using a secure session initiation protocol.

title: Control: ism-0547
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Protecting video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony traffic
text: Video conferencing and IP telephony calls are conducted using a secure real-time transport protocol.

title: Control: ism-0554
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Video conferencing unit and Internet Protocol phone authentication
text: An encrypted and non-replayable two-way authentication scheme is used for call authentication and authorisation.

title: Control: ism-0553
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Video conferencing unit and Internet Protocol phone authentication
text: Authentication and authorisation is used for all actions on a video conferencing network, including call setup and changing settings.

title: Control: ism-0555
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Video conferencing unit and Internet Protocol phone authentication
text: Authentication and authorisation is used for all actions on an IP telephony network, including registering a new IP phone, changing phone users, changing settings and accessing voicemail.

title: Control: ism-0551
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Video conferencing unit and Internet Protocol phone authentication
text:
IP telephony is configured such that:

- IP phones authenticate themselves to the call controller upon registration
- auto-registration is disabled and only authorised devices are allowed to access the network
- unauthorised devices are blocked by default
- all unused and prohibited functionality is disabled.

title: Control: ism-1014
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Video conferencing unit and Internet Protocol phone authentication
text: Individual logins are implemented for IP phones used for SECRET or TOP SECRET conversations.

title: Control: ism-0549
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Traffic separation
text: Video conferencing and IP telephony traffic is physically or logically separated from other data traffic.

title: Control: ism-0556
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Traffic separation
text: Workstations are not connected to video conferencing units or IP phones unless the workstation or the device uses virtual local area networks or similar mechanisms to maintain separation between video conferencing, IP telephony and other data traffic.

title: Control: ism-0558
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Internet Protocol phones in public areas
text: IP phones used in public areas do not have the ability to access data networks, voicemail and directory services.

title: Control: ism-0559
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Microphones and webcams
text: Microphones (including headsets and USB handsets) and webcams are not used with non-SECRET workstations in SECRET areas.

title: Control: ism-1450
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Microphones and webcams
text: Microphones (including headsets and USB handsets) and webcams are not used with non-TOP SECRET workstations in TOP SECRET areas.

title: Control: ism-1019
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Denial of service response plan
text: A denial of service response plan for video conferencing and IP telephony services is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1805
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Denial of service response plan
text:
A denial of service response plan for video conferencing and IP telephony services contains the following:

- how to identify signs of a denial-of-service attack
- how to identify the source of a denial-of-service attack
- how capabilities can be maintained during a denial-of-service attack
- what actions can be taken to respond to a denial-of-service attack.

title: Control: ism-0588
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Multifunction device usage policy
text: An MFD usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0245
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Connecting multifunction devices to digital telephone systems
text: MFDs are not connected to digital telephone systems.

title: Control: ism-1854
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Authenticating to multifunction devices
text: Human users authenticate to MFDs before they can print, scan or copy documents.

title: Control: ism-0590
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Authenticating to multifunction devices
text: Authentication measures for MFDs are the same strength as those used for workstations on networks they are connected to.

title: Control: ism-0589
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Scanning and copying documents on multifunction devices
text: MFDs are not used to scan or copy documents above the sensitivity or classification of networks they are connected to.

title: Control: ism-1855
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Logging multifunction device use
text: Use of MFDs for printing, scanning and copying purposes, including the capture of shadow copies of documents, are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-1036
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Observing multifunction device use
text: MFDs are placed in areas where their use can be observed.

title: Control: ism-2075
section: Guidelines for communications systems / Fax machines and services / Sending and receiving fax messages
text: Fax machines, and online fax services, are not used for sending or receiving fax messages.

title: Control: ism-1297
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers
text: Legal advice is sought prior to allowing privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers to access systems or data.

title: Control: ism-1400
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers
text: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data have enforced separation of classified data and personal data.

title: Control: ism-1866
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers
text: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data are prevented from storing classified data on their privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers.

title: Control: ism-2095
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers
text: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data are disallowed from granting access to unapproved artificial intelligence agents.

title: Control: ism-0694
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers
text: Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers do not access SECRET and TOP SECRET systems or data.

title: Control: ism-1482
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Organisation-owned mobile devices and desktop computers
text: Personnel using organisation-owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access classified systems or data have enforced separation of classified data and personal data.

title: Control: ism-0874
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Mobile devices and desktop computers accessing the internet
text: Mobile devices and desktop computers access the internet via an organisation’s internet gateway rather than via a direct connection to the internet.

title: Control: ism-0705
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Mobile devices and desktop computers accessing the internet
text: When accessing an organisation’s network via a VPN connection, split tunnelling is disabled.

title: Control: ism-1533
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Mobile device management policy
text: A mobile device management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1195
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Mobile device management policy
text: Mobile Device Management solutions that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against the Protection Profile for Mobile Device Management, version 4.0 or later, are used to enforce mobile device management policy.

title: Control: ism-1867
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Approved mobile platforms
text: Mobile devices that access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data use mobile platforms that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against the Protection Profile for Mobile Device Fundamentals, version 3.3 or later, and are operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated ASD security configuration guide.

title: Control: ism-0687
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Approved mobile platforms
text: Mobile devices that access SECRET or TOP SECRET systems or data use mobile platforms that have been issued an Approval for Use by ASD and are operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated Australian Communications Security Instruction.

title: Control: ism-0869
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Encrypted storage
text: Mobile devices encrypt their internal storage and any removable media using ASD-approved cryptography.

title: Control: ism-1868
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Encrypted storage
text: SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices do not use removable media unless approved beforehand by ASD.

title: Control: ism-1085
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Encrypted communications
text: Mobile devices encrypt all sensitive or classified data communicated over public network infrastructure using ASD-approved cryptography.

title: Control: ism-2108
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Encrypted communications
text: Mobile applications encrypt all sensitive or classified data communicated over public network infrastructure using ASD-approved cryptography.

title: Control: ism-1886
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Mobile devices are configured to operate in a supervised (or equivalent) mode.

title: Control: ism-2096
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Mobile devices are configured to enforce separation between organisational and personal mobile applications and data.

title: Control: ism-2097
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Mobile devices are configured with always on VPN functionality.

title: Control: ism-1887
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Mobile devices are configured with remote locate and wipe functionality.

title: Control: ism-1888
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Mobile devices are configured with secure password-based lock screens.

title: Control: ism-2098
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Mobile devices are configured to prevent data transfers over Universal Serial Bus connections.

title: Control: ism-0863
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Mobile devices prevent personnel from installing non-approved applications once provisioned.

title: Control: ism-0864
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Mobile devices prevent personnel from disabling or modifying security functionality once provisioned.

title: Control: ism-1366
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security
text: Security updates are applied to mobile devices as soon as they become available.

title: Control: ism-1082
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Mobile device usage policy
text: A mobile device usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1083
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Personnel awareness
text: Personnel are advised of the sensitivity or classification permitted for voice and data communications when using mobile devices.

title: Control: ism-1299
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Personnel awareness
text:
Personnel are advised to take the following precautions when using mobile devices:

- never leave mobile devices or removable media unattended, including by placing them in checked-in luggage or leaving them in hotel safes
- never store credentials with mobile devices that they grant access to, such as in laptop computer bags
- never lend mobile devices or removable media to untrusted people, even if briefly
- never allow untrusted people to connect their mobile devices or removable media to your mobile devices, including for charging
- never connect mobile devices to designated charging stations or wall outlet charging ports
- never use gifted or unauthorised peripherals, chargers or removable media with mobile devices
- never use removable media for data transfers or backups that have not been checked for malicious code beforehand
- avoid reuse of removable media once used with other parties’ systems or mobile devices
- avoid connecting mobile devices to open or untrusted Wi-Fi networks
- consider disabling any communications capabilities of mobile devices when not in use, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Near Field Communication and ultra-wideband
- consider periodically rebooting mobile devices
- consider using a VPN connection to encrypt all cellular and wireless communications
- consider using encrypted email or messaging apps for all communications.

title: Control: ism-0240
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using paging, message services and messaging apps
text: Paging, Multimedia Message Service, Short Message Service and messaging apps are not used to communicate sensitive or classified data.

title: Control: ism-1196
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality
text: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices are configured to remain undiscoverable to other Bluetooth devices except during Bluetooth pairing.

title: Control: ism-1200
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality
text: Bluetooth pairing for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices is performed using Secure Connections, preferably with Numeric Comparison if supported.

title: Control: ism-1198
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality
text: Bluetooth pairing for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices is performed in a manner such that connections are only made between intended Bluetooth devices.

title: Control: ism-1199
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality
text: Bluetooth pairings for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices are removed when there is no longer a requirement for their use.

title: Control: ism-0682
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality
text: Bluetooth functionality is not enabled on SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices.

title: Control: ism-2099
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Connecting mobile devices to connected vehicles
text: Mobile devices are not connected to the infotainment systems of connected vehicles.

title: Control: ism-2100
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices within or near connected vehicles
text: Sensitive or classified data is not viewed on mobile devices within or near connected vehicles.

title: Control: ism-2101
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices within or near connected vehicles
text: Sensitive or classified phone calls and conversations are not conducted within or near connected vehicles.

title: Control: ism-0866
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices in public spaces
text: Sensitive or classified data is not viewed on mobile devices in public locations unless care is taken to reduce the chance of the screen of a mobile device being observed.

title: Control: ism-1145
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices in public spaces
text: Privacy filters are applied to the screens of SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices.

title: Control: ism-1644
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices in public spaces
text: Sensitive or classified phone calls and conversations are not conducted in public locations unless care is taken to reduce the chance of conversations being overheard.

title: Control: ism-0871
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Maintaining control of mobile devices
text: Mobile devices are kept under continual direct supervision when being actively used.

title: Control: ism-0870
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Maintaining control of mobile devices
text: Mobile devices are carried or stored in a secured state when not being actively used.

title: Control: ism-1084
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Maintaining control of mobile devices
text: If unable to carry or store mobile devices in a secured state, they are physically transferred in a security briefcase or an approved multi-use satchel, pouch or transit bag.

title: Control: ism-0701
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures
text: Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes, and supporting mobile device emergency sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0702
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures
text: If a cryptographic zeroise or sanitise function is provided for cryptographic keys on a SECRET or TOP SECRET mobile device, the function is used as part of mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures.

title: Control: ism-1298
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Before travelling overseas with mobile devices
text: Personnel are advised of privacy and security risks when travelling overseas with mobile devices.

title: Control: ism-1554
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Before travelling overseas with mobile devices
text:
If travelling overseas with mobile devices to high or extreme risk countries, personnel are:

- issued with newly provisioned user accounts, mobile devices and removable media from a pool of dedicated travel devices which are used solely for work-related activities
- advised on how to apply and inspect tamper seals to key areas of mobile devices
- advised to avoid taking any personal mobile devices, especially if rooted or jailbroken.

title: Control: ism-1555
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Before travelling overseas with mobile devices
text:
Before travelling overseas with mobile devices, personnel take the following actions:

- record all details of the mobile devices being taken, such as product types, serial numbers and International Mobile Equipment Identity numbers
- update all operating systems and applications
- remove all non-essential data, applications and user accounts
- backup all remaining data, applications and settings.

title: Control: ism-1088
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / While travelling overseas with mobile devices
text:
Personnel report the potential compromise of mobile devices, removable media or credentials to their organisation as soon as possible, especially if they:

- provide credentials to foreign government officials
- decrypt mobile devices for foreign government officials
- have mobile devices taken out of sight by foreign government officials
- have mobile devices or removable media stolen, including if later returned
- lose mobile devices or removable media, including if later found
- observe unusual behaviour of mobile devices.

title: Control: ism-1300
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / After travelling overseas with mobile devices
text:
Upon returning from travelling overseas with mobile devices, personnel take the following actions:

- sanitise and reset mobile devices, including all removable media
- decommission any credentials that left their possession during their travel
- report if significant doubt exists as to the integrity of any mobile devices or removable media.

title: Control: ism-1556
section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / After travelling overseas with mobile devices
text:
If returning from travelling overseas with mobile devices to high or extreme risk countries, personnel take the following additional actions:

- reset credentials used with mobile devices, including those used for remote access to their organisation’s systems
- monitor user accounts for any indicators of compromise, such as failed logon attempts.

title: Control: ism-0280
section: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product procurement / Evaluated product selection
text: If procuring an evaluated product, a product that has completed a PP-based evaluation, including against all applicable PP modules (as well as a software bill of materials assessment if applicable), is selected in preference to one that has completed an EAL-based evaluation.

title: Control: ism-0285
section: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product procurement / Delivery of evaluated products
text: Evaluated products are delivered in a manner consistent with any delivery procedures defined in associated evaluation documentation.

title: Control: ism-0286
section: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product procurement / Delivery of evaluated products
text: When procuring high assurance information technology (IT) equipment, ASD is contacted for any equipment-specific delivery procedures.

title: Control: ism-0289
section: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product usage / Using evaluated products
text: Evaluated products are installed, configured, administered and operated in an evaluated configuration and in accordance with vendor guidance.

title: Control: ism-0290
section: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product usage / Using evaluated products
text: High assurance IT equipment is installed, configured, administered and operated in an evaluated configuration and in accordance with ASD guidance.

title: Control: ism-1551
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / IT equipment management policy
text: An IT equipment management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1913
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Hardening IT equipment configurations
text: Approved configurations for IT equipment are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1858
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Hardening IT equipment configurations
text: IT equipment is hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur.

title: Control: ism-0336
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / IT equipment registers
text: A networked IT equipment register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-1869
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / IT equipment registers
text: A non-networked IT equipment register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-0294
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Labelling IT equipment
text: IT equipment, except for high assurance IT equipment, is labelled with protective markings reflecting its sensitivity or classification.

title: Control: ism-0296
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Labelling high assurance IT equipment
text: ASD’s approval is sought before applying labels to external surfaces of high assurance IT equipment.

title: Control: ism-0293
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Classifying IT equipment
text: IT equipment is classified based on the highest sensitivity or classification of data that it is approved for processing, storing or communicating.

title: Control: ism-1599
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Handling IT equipment
text: IT equipment is handled in a manner suitable for its sensitivity or classification.

title: Control: ism-1079
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / Maintenance or repairs of high assurance IT equipment
text: ASD’s approval is sought before undertaking any maintenance or repairs to high assurance IT equipment.

title: Control: ism-0305
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / On-site maintenance or repairs
text: Maintenance or repairs of IT equipment are carried out on site by an appropriately cleared technician.

title: Control: ism-0307
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / On-site maintenance or repairs
text: If an appropriately cleared technician is not used to undertake maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, the IT equipment and associated media are sanitised before maintenance or repairs.

title: Control: ism-0306
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / On-site maintenance or repairs
text:
If an appropriately cleared technician is not used to undertake maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, the technician is escorted by someone who:

- has the authority to direct the technician
- is appropriately cleared and briefed
- is sufficiently familiar with the IT equipment to understand the work being undertaken
- takes all responsible measures to ensure the integrity of the IT equipment
- takes due care to ensure that data is not disclosed.

title: Control: ism-0310
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / Off-site maintenance or repairs
text: IT equipment maintained or repaired off site is handled at facilities approved for handling the sensitivity or classification of the IT equipment.

title: Control: ism-1598
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / Inspection of IT equipment following maintenance or repairs
text: Following maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, it is inspected to confirm that it retains its approved configuration and that no unauthorised modifications have been made.

title: Control: ism-0313
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / IT equipment sanitisation processes and procedures
text: IT equipment sanitisation processes, and supporting IT equipment sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1741
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / IT equipment destruction processes and procedures
text: IT equipment destruction processes, and supporting IT equipment destruction procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0311
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising IT equipment
text: IT equipment containing media is sanitised by removing the media from the IT equipment or by sanitising the media in situ.

title: Control: ism-1742
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising IT equipment
text: IT equipment that cannot be sanitised is destroyed.

title: Control: ism-1218
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising highly sensitive IT equipment
text: IT equipment, including associated media, that is located overseas and has processed, stored or communicated AUSTEO or AGAO data, is sanitised in situ.

title: Control: ism-0312
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising highly sensitive IT equipment
text: IT equipment, including associated media, that is located overseas and has processed, stored or communicated AUSTEO or AGAO data that cannot be sanitised in situ, is returned to Australia for destruction.

title: Control: ism-0315
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Destroying high assurance IT equipment
text: High assurance IT equipment is destroyed prior to its disposal.

title: Control: ism-0317
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices
text: At least three pages of random text with no blank areas are printed on each colour printer cartridge or MFD print drum.

title: Control: ism-1219
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices
text: MFD print drums and image transfer rollers are inspected and destroyed if there is remnant toner that cannot be removed or a print is visible on the image transfer roller.

title: Control: ism-1220
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices
text: Printer and MFD platens are inspected and destroyed if any text or images are retained on the platen.

title: Control: ism-1221
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices
text: Printers and MFDs are checked to ensure no pages are trapped in the paper path due to a paper jam.

title: Control: ism-0318
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices
text: When unable to sanitise printer cartridges or MFD print drums, they are destroyed as per electrostatic memory devices.

title: Control: ism-1534
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices
text: Printer ribbons in printers and MFDs are removed and destroyed.

title: Control: ism-1076
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising televisions and computer monitors
text: Televisions and computer monitors with minor burn-in or image persistence are sanitised by displaying a solid white image on the screen for an extended period.

title: Control: ism-1222
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising televisions and computer monitors
text: Televisions and computer monitors that cannot be sanitised are destroyed.

title: Control: ism-1223
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising network devices
text:
Memory in network devices is sanitised using the following processes, in order of preference:

- following device-specific guidance provided in evaluation documentation
- following vendor sanitisation guidance
- loading a dummy configuration file, performing a factory reset and then reinstalling firmware.

title: Control: ism-1550
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment disposal / IT equipment disposal processes and procedures
text: IT equipment disposal processes, and supporting IT equipment disposal procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1217
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment disposal / Disposal of IT equipment
text: Labels and markings indicating the owner, sensitivity, classification or any other marking that can associate IT equipment with its prior use are removed prior to its disposal.

title: Control: ism-0321
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment disposal / Disposal of IT equipment
text: When disposing of IT equipment that has been designed or modified to meet emanation security standards, ASD is contacted for requirements relating to its disposal.

title: Control: ism-0316
section: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment disposal / Disposal of IT equipment
text: Following sanitisation, destruction or declassification, a formal administrative decision is made to release IT equipment, or its waste, into the public domain.

title: Control: ism-1549
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Media management policy
text: A media management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1359
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Removable media usage policy
text: A removable media usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1713
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Removable media register
text: A removable media register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-0332
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Labelling media
text: Media, except for internally mounted fixed media within information technology equipment, is labelled with protective markings reflecting its sensitivity or classification.

title: Control: ism-0323
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Classifying media
text: Media is classified to the highest sensitivity or classification of data it stores, unless the media has been classified to a higher sensitivity or classification.

title: Control: ism-0337
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Classifying media
text: Media is only used with systems that are authorised to process, store or communicate its sensitivity or classification.

title: Control: ism-0325
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Reclassifying media
text: Any media connected to a system with a higher sensitivity or classification than the media is reclassified to the higher sensitivity or classification, unless the media is read-only or the system has a mechanism through which read-only access can be ensured.

title: Control: ism-0330
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Reclassifying media
text: Before reclassifying media to a lower sensitivity or classification, the media is sanitised or destroyed, and a formal administrative decision is made to reclassify it.

title: Control: ism-1059
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Encrypting media
text: All data stored on media is encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.

title: Control: ism-0459
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Encrypting media
text: Full disk encryption, or partial encryption where access controls only allow writing to encrypted partitions or volumes, is implemented when encrypting media.

title: Control: ism-2109
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Encrypting media
text: Pre-boot authentication using passwords, or managed network-based key release, is implemented for media containing encrypted system volumes.

title: Control: ism-0831
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Handling media
text: Media is handled in a manner suitable for its sensitivity or classification.

title: Control: ism-1600
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Sanitising media before first use
text: Media is sanitised before it is used for the first time.

title: Control: ism-1642
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Sanitising media before first use
text: Media is sanitised before it is reused in a different security domain.

title: Control: ism-0347
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Using media for data transfers
text: When transferring data manually between two systems belonging to different security domains, write-once media is used unless the destination system has a mechanism through which read-only access can be ensured.

title: Control: ism-0947
section: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Using media for data transfers
text: When transferring data manually between two systems belonging to different security domains, rewritable media is sanitised after each data transfer.

title: Control: ism-0348
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Media sanitisation processes and procedures
text: Media sanitisation processes, and supporting media sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0351
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Volatile media sanitisation
text: Volatile media is sanitised by removing its power for at least 10 minutes.

title: Control: ism-0352
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Volatile media sanitisation
text: SECRET and TOP SECRET volatile media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.

title: Control: ism-0835
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Treatment of volatile media following sanitisation
text: Following sanitisation, TOP SECRET volatile media retains its classification if it stored static data for an extended period, or had data repeatedly stored on or written to the same memory location for an extended period.

title: Control: ism-0354
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation
text: Non-volatile magnetic media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once (or three times if pre-2001 or under 15 GB) in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.

title: Control: ism-1065
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation
text: The host-protected area and device configuration overlay table are reset prior to the sanitisation of non-volatile magnetic hard drives.

title: Control: ism-1067
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation
text: The ATA secure erase command is used, in addition to block overwriting software, to ensure the growth defects table of non-volatile magnetic hard drives is overwritten.

title: Control: ism-0356
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Treatment of non-volatile magnetic media following sanitisation
text: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile magnetic media retains its classification.

title: Control: ism-0357
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile erasable programmable read-only memory media sanitisation
text: Non-volatile EPROM media is sanitised by applying three times the manufacturer’s specified ultraviolet erasure time and then overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.

title: Control: ism-0836
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile electrically erasable programmable read-only memory media sanitisation
text: Non-volatile EEPROM media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.

title: Control: ism-0358
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Treatment of non-volatile erasable and electrically erasable programmable read-only memory media following sanitisation
text: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile EPROM and EEPROM media retains its classification.

title: Control: ism-0359
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile flash memory media sanitisation
text: Non-volatile flash memory media is sanitised by overwriting it at least twice in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.

title: Control: ism-0360
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Treatment of non-volatile flash memory media following sanitisation
text: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile flash memory media retains its classification.

title: Control: ism-1735
section: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Media that cannot be successfully sanitised
text: Media that cannot be successfully sanitised is destroyed prior to its disposal.

title: Control: ism-0363
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction processes and procedures
text: Media destruction processes, and supporting media destruction procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0350
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media that cannot be sanitised
text:
The following media types are destroyed prior to their disposal:

- microfiche and microfilm
- optical discs
- programmable read-only memory
- read-only memory
- other types of media that cannot be sanitised.

title: Control: ism-1361
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction equipment
text: Security Construction and Equipment Committee-approved equipment or ASIO-approved equipment is used when destroying media.

title: Control: ism-1160
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction equipment
text: If using degaussers to destroy media, degaussers evaluated by the United States’ National Security Agency are used.

title: Control: ism-1517
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods
text: Equipment that is capable of reducing microform to a fine powder, with resultant particles not showing more than five consecutive characters per particle upon microscopic inspection, is used to destroy microfiche and microfilm.

title: Control: ism-1722
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods
text: Electrostatic memory devices are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator or grinder/sander.

title: Control: ism-1723
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods
text: Magnetic floppy disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, degausser or by cutting.

title: Control: ism-1724
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods
text: Magnetic hard disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or degausser.

title: Control: ism-1725
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods
text: Magnetic tapes are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, degausser or by cutting.

title: Control: ism-1726
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods
text: Optical disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or by cutting.

title: Control: ism-1727
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods
text: Semiconductor memory is destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill or disintegrator.

title: Control: ism-0368
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods
text: Media destroyed using a hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or by cutting results in media waste particles no larger than 9 mm.

title: Control: ism-1728
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Treatment of media waste particles
text: The resulting media waste particles from the destruction of SECRET media is stored and handled as OFFICIAL if less than or equal to 3 mm, PROTECTED if greater than 3 mm and less than or equal to 6 mm, or SECRET if greater than 6 mm and less than or equal to 9 mm.

title: Control: ism-1729
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Treatment of media waste particles
text: The resulting media waste particles from the destruction of TOP SECRET media is stored and handled as OFFICIAL if less than or equal to 3 mm, or SECRET if greater than 3 mm and less than or equal to 9 mm.

title: Control: ism-0361
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Degaussing magnetic media
text: Magnetic media is destroyed using a degausser with a suitable magnetic field strength and magnetic orientation.

title: Control: ism-0362
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Degaussing magnetic media
text: Product-specific directions provided by degausser manufacturers are followed.

title: Control: ism-1641
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Degaussing magnetic media
text: Following the use of a degausser, magnetic media is physically damaged by deforming any internal platters.

title: Control: ism-0370
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Supervision of destruction
text: The destruction of media is performed under the supervision of at least one cleared person.

title: Control: ism-0371
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Supervision of destruction
text: Personnel supervising the destruction of media supervise its handling to the point of destruction and ensure that the destruction is completed successfully.

title: Control: ism-0372
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Supervision of accountable material destruction
text: The destruction of media storing accountable material is performed under the supervision of at least two cleared personnel.

title: Control: ism-0373
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Supervision of accountable material destruction
text: Personnel supervising the destruction of media storing accountable material supervise its handling to the point of destruction, ensure that the destruction is completed successfully and sign a destruction certificate afterwards.

title: Control: ism-0839
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Outsourcing media destruction
text: The destruction of media storing accountable material is not outsourced.

title: Control: ism-0840
section: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Outsourcing media destruction
text: When outsourcing the destruction of media storing non-accountable material, a National Association for Information Destruction AAA certified destruction service with endorsements, as specified in ASIO’s Protective Security Circular-167, is used.

title: Control: ism-0374
section: Guidelines for media / Media disposal / Media disposal processes and procedures
text: Media disposal processes, and supporting media disposal procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0378
section: Guidelines for media / Media disposal / Disposal of media
text: Labels and markings indicating the owner, sensitivity, classification or any other marking that can associate media with its prior use are removed prior to its disposal.

title: Control: ism-0375
section: Guidelines for media / Media disposal / Disposal of media
text: Following sanitisation, destruction or declassification, a formal administrative decision is made to release media, or its waste, into the public domain.

title: Control: ism-1743
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Operating system selection
text: Vendors that have demonstrated a commitment to Secure by Design and Secure by Default principles and practices, including secure programming practices and either memory-safe programming languages or less preferably memory-safe programming practices, are used for operating systems.

title: Control: ism-1407
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Operating system releases and versions
text: The latest release, or the previous release, of operating systems are used.

title: Control: ism-1408
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Operating system releases and versions
text: 64-bit versions of operating systems are used.

title: Control: ism-1406
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Standard operating environments
text: SOEs are used for workstations and servers.

title: Control: ism-1608
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Standard operating environments
text: SOEs provided by third parties are scanned for malicious code and configurations.

title: Control: ism-1588
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Standard operating environments
text: SOEs are reviewed and updated at least annually.

title: Control: ism-1914
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Approved configurations for operating systems are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1409
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Operating systems are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur.

title: Control: ism-1601
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Microsoft’s attack surface reduction rules are implemented.

title: Control: ism-0383
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Default user accounts or credentials for operating systems, including for any pre-configured user accounts, are changed, disabled or removed during initial setup.

title: Control: ism-0380
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Unneeded user accounts, components, services and functionality of operating systems are disabled or removed.

title: Control: ism-0341
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Automatic execution features for removable media are disabled.

title: Control: ism-1654
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Internet Explorer 11 is disabled or removed.

title: Control: ism-1655
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: .NET Framework 3.5 (includes .NET 2.0 and 3.0) is disabled or removed.

title: Control: ism-1492
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Operating system exploit protection functionality is enabled.

title: Control: ism-1745
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Early Launch Antimalware, Secure Boot, Trusted Boot and Measured Boot functionality is enabled.

title: Control: ism-2127
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Digital signature verification functionality for drivers is enforced before they are loaded.

title: Control: ism-1896
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Memory integrity functionality is enabled.

title: Control: ism-2128
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: The ability to install, load or modify kernel-mode code, including drivers, kernel modules and extensions, is limited to privileged users who require such abilities as part of their duties or functions.

title: Control: ism-1584
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text: Unprivileged users are prevented from bypassing, disabling or modifying security functionality of operating systems.

title: Control: ism-1491
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations
text:
Unprivileged human users are prevented from running script execution engines, including:

- Windows Script Host (cscript.exe and wscript.exe)
- PowerShell (powershell.exe, powershell_ise.exe and pwsh.exe)
- Command Prompt (cmd.exe)
- Windows Management Instrumentation (wmic.exe)
- Microsoft Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) Application Host (mshta.exe).

title: Control: ism-1592
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application management
text: Unprivileged human users do not have the ability to install unapproved applications.

title: Control: ism-0382
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application management
text: Unprivileged human users do not have the ability to uninstall or disable approved applications.

title: Control: ism-0843
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Application control is implemented on workstations.

title: Control: ism-1490
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Application control is implemented on internet-facing servers.

title: Control: ism-1656
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Application control is implemented on non-internet-facing servers.

title: Control: ism-1870
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Application control is applied to user profiles and temporary folders used by operating systems, web browsers and email clients.

title: Control: ism-1871
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Application control is applied to all locations other than user profiles and temporary folders used by operating systems, web browsers and email clients.

title: Control: ism-1657
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Application control restricts the execution of executables, libraries, scripts, installers, compiled HTML, HTML applications and control panel applets to an organisation-approved set.

title: Control: ism-1658
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Application control restricts the execution of drivers to an organisation-approved set.

title: Control: ism-0955
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Application control is implemented using cryptographic hash rules, publisher certificate rules or path rules.

title: Control: ism-1471
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: When implementing application control using publisher certificate rules, publisher names and product names are used.

title: Control: ism-1392
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: When implementing application control using path rules, only approved users can modify approved files and write to approved folders.

title: Control: ism-1746
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: When implementing application control using path rules, only approved users can change file system permissions for approved files and folders.

title: Control: ism-1544
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control
text: Microsoft’s recommended application blocklist is implemented.

title: Control: ism-1659
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Application control

title: Control: ism-1417
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Antivirus application
text:
An antivirus application is implemented on workstations and servers with:

- signature-based detection functionality enabled and set to a high level
- heuristic-based detection functionality enabled and set to a high level
- reputation rating functionality enabled
- ransomware protection functionality enabled
- detection signatures configured to update at least daily
- regular scanning configured for all fixed disks and removable media.

section: Guidelines for system hardening / Server application hardening / Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services account hardening

title: Control: ism-1844
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Server application hardening / Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services account hardening
text: Computer accounts that are not Microsoft AD DS domain controllers are not trusted for delegation to services.

title: Control: ism-1460
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Virtualisation hardening / Functional separation between operating environments
text: When using a software-based isolation mechanism that consumes shared physical computing resources, the isolation mechanism is from a vendor that has demonstrated a commitment to Secure by Design and Secure by Default principles and practices, including secure programming practices and either memory-safe programming languages or less preferably memory-safe programming practices.

title: Control: ism-1604
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Virtualisation hardening / Functional separation between operating environments

title: Control: ism-1605

title: Control: ism-1606
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Virtualisation hardening / Functional separation between operating environments

section: Guidelines for system hardening / Virtualisation hardening / Functional separation between operating environments

title: Control: ism-1607
section: Guidelines for system hardening / Virtualisation hardening / Functional separation between operating environments
