text: Unique privileged user accounts are used for administering individual server applications.

title: Control: ism-1509
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Privileged access to systems
text: Privileged access events are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-1650
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Privileged access to systems
text: Privileged user account and security group management events are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-0446
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Privileged access to systems by foreign nationals
text: Foreign nationals, including seconded foreign nationals, do not have privileged access to systems that process, store or communicate AUSTEO or REL data.

title: Control: ism-0447
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Privileged access to systems by foreign nationals
text: Foreign nationals, excluding seconded foreign nationals, do not have privileged access to systems that process, store or communicate AGAO data.

title: Control: ism-0407
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Recording authorisation for personnel to access systems
text:
A secure record is maintained for the life of systems and their resources that covers the following for each human user:

- their unique identifier
- their signed agreement to abide by system usage policies
- who authorised their access
- when their access was granted
- the level of access they were granted
- when their access, and their level of access, was last reviewed
- when their level of access was changed, and to what extent (if applicable)
- when their access was withdrawn (if applicable).

title: Control: ism-2134
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Artificial intelligence agent register
text: An AI agent register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-2135
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Artificial intelligence agent register
text:
An AI agent register contains the following for each AI agent:

- its unique identifier
- its owner and business purpose
- the identities assigned to it
- any user accounts and credentials it uses
- the tools, permissions and data repositories it can access.

title: Control: ism-0430
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Suspension of access to systems
text: Access to systems and their resources are removed or suspended the same day users no longer have a legitimate requirement for access.

title: Control: ism-1591
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Suspension of access to systems
text: Access to systems and their resources are removed or suspended as soon as practicable when users are detected undertaking malicious activities.

title: Control: ism-1404
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Suspension of access to systems
text: Unprivileged access to systems and their resources are disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

title: Control: ism-1648
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Suspension of access to systems
text: Privileged access to systems and their resources are disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

title: Control: ism-1647
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Suspension of access to systems
text: Privileged access to systems and their resources are disabled after 12 months unless revalidated.

title: Control: ism-0441
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Temporary access to systems
text: When personnel are granted temporary access to systems and their resources, effective security controls are put in place to restrict their access to only data required for them to undertake their duties or functions.

title: Control: ism-0443
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Temporary access to systems
text: Temporary access is not granted to systems that process, store or communicate caveated or sensitive compartmented information.

title: Control: ism-1610
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Emergency access to systems
text: A method of emergency access to systems and their resources is documented and tested at least once when initially implemented and each time fundamental information technology infrastructure changes occur.

title: Control: ism-1611
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Emergency access to systems
text: Break glass accounts are only used when normal authentication processes cannot be used.

title: Control: ism-1612
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Emergency access to systems
text: Break glass accounts are only used for specific authorised activities.

title: Control: ism-1614
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Emergency access to systems
text: Break glass account credentials are changed by the account custodian after they are accessed by any other party.

title: Control: ism-1615
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Emergency access to systems
text: Break glass accounts are tested after credentials are changed.

title: Control: ism-1613
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Emergency access to systems
text: Use of break glass accounts is centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-0078
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Control of Australian systems
text: Systems processing, storing or communicating AUSTEO or AGAO data remain at all times under the control of an Australian national working for or on behalf of the Australian Government.

title: Control: ism-0854
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Control of Australian systems
text: AUSTEO and AGAO data can only be accessed from systems under the sole control of the Australian Government that are located within facilities authorised by the Australian Government.

title: Control: ism-1546
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Authenticating to systems
text: Users are authenticated before they are granted access to a system and its resources.

title: Control: ism-2136
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Authenticating to systems
text: Risk-based access decisions, informed by contextual signals, are enforced for access to systems and their resources.

title: Control: ism-1603
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Insecure authentication methods
text: Authentication methods susceptible to replay attacks are disabled.

title: Control: ism-1055
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Insecure authentication methods
text: LAN Manager and NT LAN Manager authentication methods are disabled.

title: Control: ism-2076
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Insecure authentication methods
text: Security questions are not used for authentication purposes.

title: Control: ism-2077
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Insecure authentication methods
text: Email is not used for out-of-band authentication purposes.

title: Control: ism-1504
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to their organisation’s online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data.

title: Control: ism-1679
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to third-party online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data.

title: Control: ism-1680
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication (where available) is used to authenticate human users to third-party online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s non-sensitive data.

title: Control: ism-1892
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to their organisation’s online customer services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive customer data.

title: Control: ism-1893
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to third-party online customer services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive customer data.

title: Control: ism-1681
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate customers to online customer services that process, store or communicate sensitive customer data.

title: Control: ism-1919
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: When multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users or customers to online services or online customer services, all other authentication protocols that do not support multi-factor authentication are disabled.

title: Control: ism-1173
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate privileged human users of systems.

title: Control: ism-0974
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate unprivileged human users of systems.

title: Control: ism-1505
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users of data repositories.

title: Control: ism-1401
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication uses either: something people have and something people know, or something people have that is unlocked by something people know or are.

title: Control: ism-1872
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication used for authenticating human users of online services is phishing-resistant.

title: Control: ism-1873
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication used for authenticating customers of online customer services provides a phishing-resistant option.

title: Control: ism-1874
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication used for authenticating customers of online customer services is phishing-resistant.

title: Control: ism-1682
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication used for authenticating human users of systems is phishing-resistant.

title: Control: ism-1894
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Multi-factor authentication used for authenticating human users of data repositories is phishing-resistant.

title: Control: ism-2011
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: When phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication is used by human users, other non-phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication options are disabled for their user accounts.

title: Control: ism-1920
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: When multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to online services, online customer services, systems or data repositories  -  that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data or sensitive customer data  -  human users are prevented from self-enrolling into multi-factor authentication from untrustworthy devices.

title: Control: ism-1683
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Multi-factor authentication
text: Successful and unsuccessful multi-factor authentication events are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-0417
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Single-factor authentication
text: When systems cannot support multi-factor authentication, single-factor authentication using passwords is implemented instead.

title: Control: ism-1895
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Single-factor authentication
text: Successful and unsuccessful single-factor authentication events are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-1403
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / User account lockouts
text: User accounts, except for break glass accounts, are protected by fixed or risk-based lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts, with either indefinite or automated lockout durations.

title: Control: ism-0428
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Session locking
text:
Services are configured with a session lock that:

- activates after a maximum of 15 minutes of human user inactivity, a maximum of 12 hours of overall session time or when manually activated
- blocks access to all session content
- requires re-authentication by human users using all authentication factors to unlock the session
- denies human users the ability to disable the session locking mechanism.

title: Control: ism-2012
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Screen locking
text:
Systems are configured with a screen lock that:

- activates after a maximum of 15 minutes of human user inactivity, or when manually activated
- conceals all content on the screen
- ensures that the screen does not enter a power saving state before the screen lock is activated
- requires re-authentication by human users using all authentication factors to unlock the system
- denies human users the ability to disable the screen locking mechanism.

title: Control: ism-0853
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Session termination
text: Interactive user sessions are terminated and workstations are restarted at least daily.

title: Control: ism-2137
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Third-party application access and device code authentication
text: Human users are prevented from granting consent to third-party OAuth applications, with such consent granted only by an authorised administrator.

title: Control: ism-2138
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Third-party application access and device code authentication
text: OAuth application consents, including their granted permissions, are reviewed at least every six months, with unused applications and excessive permissions revoked.

title: Control: ism-2139
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Third-party application access and device code authentication
text: Consent grants, token issuance and token use for third-party OAuth applications are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-2140
section: Guidelines for system access / Identity and access management / Third-party application access and device code authentication
text: The OAuth device code authentication flow is disabled unless required, and where required, is restricted to authorised user accounts and managed devices.

title: Control: ism-1559
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Passwords used for multi-factor authentication on non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED systems are a minimum of 6 characters.

title: Control: ism-1560
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Passwords used for multi-factor authentication on SECRET systems are a minimum of 8 characters.

title: Control: ism-1561
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Passwords used for multi-factor authentication on TOP SECRET systems are a minimum of 10 characters.

title: Control: ism-0421
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Passwords used for single-factor authentication on non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED systems are a minimum of 15 characters.

title: Control: ism-1557
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Passwords used for single-factor authentication on SECRET systems are a minimum of 17 characters.

title: Control: ism-0422
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Passwords used for single-factor authentication on TOP SECRET systems are a minimum of 20 characters.

title: Control: ism-1558
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text:
Passwords using a sequence of words for single-factor authentication are not constructed using:

- a list of categorised words
- a real sentence in a natural language
- song lyrics, movie or television show quotes, literature, or any other publicly available material
- less than 4 random words for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED systems; 5 random words for SECRET systems; or 6 random words for TOP SECRET systems.

title: Control: ism-2078
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Passwords appearing in lists of commonly used passwords or lists of compromised passwords are not used.

title: Control: ism-2079
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Maximum length limits for passwords are not less than 64 characters.

title: Control: ism-2080
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: Password complexity requirements are not imposed for passwords.

title: Control: ism-2081
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Password strength
text: All ASCII printable characters are supported for passwords.

title: Control: ism-1593
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for user accounts
text: Human users provide sufficient evidence to verify their identity when first requesting credentials, when requesting the reset of any credentials, when requesting the temporary disabling of any credentials, and when requesting the enrolment or re-enrolment of any credentials.

title: Control: ism-1227
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for user accounts
text: Credentials set for user accounts are randomly generated.

title: Control: ism-1594
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for user accounts
text: Credentials for human users are provided via a secure communications channel or, if not possible, split into two parts with one part provided to the human user and the other part provided to their supervisor.

title: Control: ism-1595
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for user accounts
text: Credentials provided to human users are changed on first use.

title: Control: ism-1596
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for user accounts
text: Credentials are not reused by users across different systems.

title: Control: ism-1953
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for built-in Administrator accounts, break glass accounts, local administrator accounts and service accounts
text: Credentials for the built-in Administrator account in each domain are long, unique, unpredictable and managed.

title: Control: ism-1685
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for built-in Administrator accounts, break glass accounts, local administrator accounts and service accounts
text: Credentials for break glass accounts, local administrator accounts and service accounts are long, unique, unpredictable and managed.

title: Control: ism-1795
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for built-in Administrator accounts, break glass accounts, local administrator accounts and service accounts
text: Credentials for built-in Administrator accounts, break glass accounts, local administrator accounts and service accounts are a minimum of 30 characters.

title: Control: ism-1954
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for built-in Administrator accounts, break glass accounts, local administrator accounts and service accounts
text: Credentials for built-in Administrator accounts, break glass accounts, local administrator accounts and service accounts are randomly generated.

title: Control: ism-1619
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Setting credentials for built-in Administrator accounts, break glass accounts, local administrator accounts and service accounts
text: Service accounts are created as group Managed Service Accounts.

title: Control: ism-2141
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Application and workload credentials
text: Applications and workloads use short-lived dynamically issued credentials in preference to long-lived static credentials.

title: Control: ism-2142
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Application and workload credentials
text: Static credentials used by applications and workloads are centrally managed using a credential or secrets management solution.

title: Control: ism-2143
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Application and workload credentials
text: Applications and workloads use unique credentials that are not shared with other applications or workloads, or across development, testing, staging and production environments.

title: Control: ism-1590
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Changing credentials
text:
Credentials for user accounts are changed if:

- they are compromised or suspected of being compromised
- they are discovered stored on systems in the clear
- they are discovered being transferred across networks in the clear
- membership of a shared user account changes.

title: Control: ism-2144
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Changing credentials
text:
Static credentials used by applications and workloads are changed if:

- they are compromised or suspected of being compromised
- they are discovered stored on systems in the clear
- they are discovered being transferred across networks in the clear.

title: Control: ism-1955
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Changing credentials
text: Credentials for computer accounts are changed if they are compromised, they are suspected of being compromised or they have not been changed in the past 30 days.

title: Control: ism-1847
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Changing credentials
text: Credentials for the Kerberos Key Distribution Center’s service account (KRBTGT) are changed twice, allowing for replication to all Microsoft AD DS domain controllers in-between each change, if the domain has been directly compromised, the domain is suspected of being compromised or they have not been changed in the past six months.

title: Control: ism-1956
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Changing credentials
text: Microsoft AD FS token-signing and encryption certificates are changed twice in quick succession if they are compromised, they are suspected of being compromised or they have not been changed in the past 12 months.

title: Control: ism-2145
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Revoking credentials
text: Credentials for user accounts are revoked when they are no longer required.

title: Control: ism-2146
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Revoking credentials
text: Static credentials used by applications and workloads are revoked when they are no longer required.

title: Control: ism-1597
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Credentials are obscured as they are entered into systems.

title: Control: ism-1980
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Credential hint functionality is not used for systems.

title: Control: ism-0418
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Physical credentials are kept separate from systems they are used to authenticate to, except for when performing authentication activities.

title: Control: ism-1402
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Credentials stored on systems are protected by a password manager; a hardware security module; or by salting, hashing and stretching them before storage within a database.

title: Control: ism-1957
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Private keys for Microsoft AD CS certification authority servers are protected by a hardware security module.

title: Control: ism-1861
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Local Security Authority protection functionality is enabled.

title: Control: ism-1686
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Credential Guard functionality is enabled.

title: Control: ism-1897
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Remote Credential Guard functionality is enabled.

title: Control: ism-1749
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Cached credentials are limited to one previous logon.

title: Control: ism-1875
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting credentials
text: Systems are scanned at least monthly to identify any credentials that are being stored in the clear.

title: Control: ism-2147
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting authentication artefacts
text: Authentication tokens, session cookies and refresh tokens are cryptographically bound to the device on which they were issued.

title: Control: ism-2148
section: Guidelines for system access / Credential management / Protecting authentication artefacts
text: Active sessions, refresh tokens and other authentication artefacts are revoked when credentials are reset or re-enrolled, when credentials are compromised or suspected of being compromised, when a device no longer meets compliance requirements, or when high-risk sign-in activity is detected.

title: Control: ism-0042
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / System administration processes and procedures
text: System administration processes, and supporting system administration procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1211
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / System administration processes and procedures
text: System administration activities are performed in accordance with the system’s change and configuration management plan.

title: Control: ism-1898
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Separate privileged operating environments
text: Secure Admin Workstations are used in the performance of administrative activities.

title: Control: ism-1380
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Separate privileged operating environments
text: Privileged human users use separate privileged and unprivileged operating environments.

title: Control: ism-1687
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Separate privileged operating environments
text: Privileged operating environments are not virtualised within unprivileged operating environments.

title: Control: ism-1688
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Separate privileged operating environments
text: Unprivileged user accounts cannot be used to log on to privileged operating environments.

title: Control: ism-1689
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Separate privileged operating environments
text: Privileged user accounts (excluding local administrator accounts) cannot be used to log on to unprivileged operating environments.

title: Control: ism-1958
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Separate privileged operating environments
text: User accounts with DCSync permissions cannot be used to log on to unprivileged operating environments.

title: Control: ism-1385
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Administrative infrastructure
text: Administrative infrastructure is segregated from the wider network and the internet.

title: Control: ism-1750
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Administrative infrastructure
text: Administrative infrastructure for critical servers, high-value servers and regular servers is segregated from each other.

title: Control: ism-1386
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Administrative infrastructure
text: Network management traffic can only originate from administrative infrastructure.

title: Control: ism-1387
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Administrative infrastructure
text: Administrative activities are conducted through jump servers.

title: Control: ism-1899
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Administrative infrastructure
text: Network devices that do not belong to administrative infrastructure cannot initiate connections with administrative infrastructure.

title: Control: ism-2149
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Administrative tools
text: A list of authorised RMM tools and remote access tools is developed, enforced and maintained.

title: Control: ism-2150
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Administrative tools
text: Network connections for unauthorised RMM tools and remote access tools are blocked at gateways.

title: Control: ism-1493
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Software registers
text: Software registers for workstations, servers, network devices and networked IT equipment are developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-1643
section: Guidelines for system management / System administration / Software registers
text: Software registers contain versions and patch histories of applications, drivers, operating systems and firmware.

title: Control: ism-1143
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Patch management processes and procedures
text: Patch management processes, and supporting patch management procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0298
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Patch management processes and procedures
text: A centralised and managed approach that maintains the integrity of patches or updates, and confirms that they have been applied successfully, is used to patch or update applications, operating systems, drivers and firmware.

title: Control: ism-1876
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in online services are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1690
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in online services are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1691
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF applications, and security products are applied within two weeks of release.

title: Control: ism-1692
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF applications, and security products are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1901
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF applications, and security products are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1693
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in applications other than office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF applications, and security products are applied within one month of release.

title: Control: ism-1877
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of internet-facing servers and internet-facing network devices are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1694
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of internet-facing servers and internet-facing network devices are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1695
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within one month of release.

title: Control: ism-1696
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1902
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within one month of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1878
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of IT equipment other than workstations, servers and network devices are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1751
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of IT equipment other than workstations, servers and network devices are applied within one month of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1879
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in drivers are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1697
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in drivers are applied within one month of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

title: Control: ism-1903
section: Guidelines for system management / System maintenance / Mitigating known vulnerabilities
text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in firmware are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.
