title: Control: ism-2088
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Artificial intelligence model poisoning
text: Data validation and verification techniques are used to ensure the reliability and accuracy of training data used by AI models.

title: Control: ism-2089
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Unbounded consumption
text: AI model performance metrics are monitored and anomalies are investigated.

title: Control: ism-2090
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Unbounded consumption
text: Rate limiting is applied to inference queries for AI models.

title: Control: ism-2091
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Unbounded consumption
text: Resource limits are enforced for AI models.

title: Control: ism-2092
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Excessive agency
text: Access control policies are implemented to enforce fine-grained permissions for AI applications.

title: Control: ism-2093
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Excessive agency
text: Role-based access controls are implemented for AI applications to restrict access to sensitive data.

title: Control: ism-2156
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Excessive agency
text: Agentic AI applications are restricted to the minimum set of tools, functions and permissions required for their intended purpose.

title: Control: ism-2157
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Excessive agency
text: Tools invoked by agentic AI applications are subject to both the access controls of the invoking user and agent-specific, task-scoped authorisation, with effective permissions limited to the minimum permitted by both.

title: Control: ism-2158
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Excessive agency
text: External content retrieved by agentic AI applications is treated as untrusted data throughout processing, is clearly delimited from system instructions, is subject to validation and sanitisation measures applied to other untrusted input, remains untrusted following such processing, and is prevented from modifying or overriding system instructions, security policies, access controls, tool permissions or human approval requirements.

title: Control: ism-2159
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Excessive agency
text: All tool invocations, external requests and outputs generated by agentic AI applications are centrally logged with sufficient detail to support cyber security incident investigations.

title: Control: ism-1924
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Prompt injection
text: Generative AI applications evaluate user prompts to detect and mitigate adversarial inputs or suffixes designed to elicit unintended behaviour or assist in the generation of sensitive or harmful content.

title: Control: ism-2094
section: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Sensitive data exposure and improper output
text: Content filtering is implemented by AI applications to detect and block sensitive data exposure and improper output.

title: Control: ism-1922
section: Guidelines for software development / Mobile application development / Secure mobile application development
text: The OWASP Mobile Application Security Verification Standard is used in the development of mobile applications.

title: Control: ism-1239
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: Robust web application frameworks are used in the development of web applications.

title: Control: ism-0971
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: The OWASP Application Security Verification Standard is used in the development of web applications.

title: Control: ism-1849
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: The OWASP Top 10 Proactive Controls are used in the development of web applications.

title: Control: ism-1850
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: The OWASP Top 10 are mitigated in the development of web applications.

title: Control: ism-2063
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: If supported, web application session cookies set the HttpOnly flag, Secure flag and the SameSite flag by default.

title: Control: ism-2064
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: Web application session cookies contain only digitally signed opaque bearer tokens.

title: Control: ism-2065
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: Web application session cookies using opaque bearer tokens that are not digitally signed use non-sequential random identifiers with a minimum of 128 bits of entropy, preferably 256 bits of entropy.

title: Control: ism-2066
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: Web application sessions are centrally managed server side.

title: Control: ism-2067
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development
text: Web applications that support Single Sign On equally support Single Logout.

title: Control: ism-1424
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Web security policy response headers
text: Content-Security-Policy, Hypertext Transfer Protocol Strict Transport Security and X-Frame-Options are specified by web server software via security policy in response headers.

title: Control: ism-1552
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Web application interactions
text: All web application content is offered exclusively using HTTPS.

title: Control: ism-1851
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Web application programming interfaces
text: The OWASP API Security Top 10 are mitigated in the development of web APIs.

title: Control: ism-1241
section: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Web application output encoding
text: Output encoding is performed on all output produced by web applications.

title: Control: ism-1269
section: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Functional separation between database servers and web servers
text: Database servers and web servers are functionally separated.

title: Control: ism-1277
section: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Communications between database servers and web servers
text: Data communicated between database servers and web servers is encrypted using Australian Signals Directorate-approved cryptography.

title: Control: ism-1270
section: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Network environment
text: Database servers are placed on a different network segment to workstations.

title: Control: ism-1271
section: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Network environment
text: Network access controls are implemented to restrict database server communications to strictly defined network resources that require access to the database server.

title: Control: ism-1272
section: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Network environment
text: If only local access to a database is required, networking functionality of database management system applications is disabled or directed to listen solely to the localhost interface.

title: Control: ism-1273
section: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Segregation of development, testing, staging and production database servers
text: Database servers for development, testing, staging and production environments are segregated.

title: Control: ism-1243
section: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Database register
text: A database register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

title: Control: ism-1256
section: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Protecting databases
text: File-based access controls are applied to database files.

title: Control: ism-0393
section: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Protecting database contents
text: Databases and their contents are classified based on the sensitivity or classification of data that they contain.

title: Control: ism-1255
section: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Protecting database contents
text: Database users’ ability to access, insert, modify and remove database contents is restricted based on their duties or functions.

title: Control: ism-1268
section: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Protecting database contents
text: The need-to-know principle is enforced for database contents through the application of minimum privileges, database views, database roles and data tokenisation.

title: Control: ism-1274
section: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Segregation of development, testing, staging and production databases
text: Database contents from production environments are not used in non-production environments unless the non-production environment is secured to at least the same level as the production environment.

title: Control: ism-1537
section: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Database event logging
text:
Security-relevant events for databases are centrally logged, including:

- access or modification of particularly important content
- addition of new users, especially privileged users
- changes to user roles or privileges
- attempts to elevate user privileges
- queries containing comments
- queries containing multiple embedded queries
- database and query alerts or failures
- database structure changes
- database administrator actions
- use of executable commands
- database logons and logoffs.

title: Control: ism-0264
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Email usage policy
text: An email usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0267
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Webmail services
text: Access to non-approved webmail services is blocked.

title: Control: ism-0270
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Protective markings for emails
text: Protective markings are applied to emails and reflect the highest sensitivity or classification of the subject, body and attachments.

title: Control: ism-0271
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Protective marking tools
text: Protective marking tools do not automatically insert protective markings into emails.

title: Control: ism-0272
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Protective marking tools
text: Protective marking tools do not allow the selection of protective markings that a system has not been authorised to process, store or communicate.

title: Control: ism-1089
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Protective marking tools
text: When replying to or forwarding emails, protective marking tools do not allow the selection of protective markings lower than previously used.

title: Control: ism-0565
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Handling emails with inappropriate, invalid or missing protective markings
text: Email servers are configured to block, log and report emails with inappropriate protective markings.

title: Control: ism-1023
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Handling emails with inappropriate, invalid or missing protective markings
text: The intended recipients of blocked inbound emails, and the senders of blocked outbound emails, are notified.

title: Control: ism-0269
section: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Email distribution lists
text: Emails containing Australian Eyes Only, Australian Government Access Only or Releasable To data are not sent to email distribution lists unless the nationality of all members of email distribution lists can be confirmed.

title: Control: ism-0569
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Centralised email gateways
text: Emails are routed via centralised email gateways.

title: Control: ism-0571
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Centralised email gateways
text: When users send or receive emails, an authenticated and encrypted channel is used to route emails via their organisation’s centralised email gateways.

title: Control: ism-0570
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Email gateway maintenance activities
text: Where backup or alternative email gateways are in place, they are maintained at the same standard as the primary email gateway.

title: Control: ism-0567
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Open relay email servers
text: Email servers only relay emails destined for or originating from their domains (including subdomains).

title: Control: ism-0572
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Email server transport encryption
text: Opportunistic TLS encryption is enabled on email servers that make incoming or outgoing email connections over public network infrastructure.

title: Control: ism-1589
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Email server transport encryption
text: MTA-STS is enabled to prevent the unencrypted transfer of emails between email servers.

title: Control: ism-0574
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Sender Policy Framework
text: SPF is used to specify authorised email servers (or lack thereof) for an organisation’s domains (including subdomains).

title: Control: ism-1183
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Sender Policy Framework
text: A hard fail SPF record is used when specifying authorised email servers (or lack thereof) for an organisation’s domains (including subdomains).

title: Control: ism-1151
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Sender Policy Framework
text: SPF is used to verify the authenticity of incoming emails.

title: Control: ism-0861
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / DomainKeys Identified Mail
text: DKIM signing is enabled on emails originating from an organisation’s domains (including subdomains).

title: Control: ism-1026
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / DomainKeys Identified Mail
text: DKIM signatures on incoming emails are verified.

title: Control: ism-1027
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / DomainKeys Identified Mail
text: Email distribution list applications used by external senders is configured such that it does not break the validity of the sender’s DKIM signature.

title: Control: ism-1540
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance
text: DMARC records are configured for an organisation’s domains (including subdomains) such that emails are rejected if they do not pass DMARC checks.

title: Control: ism-1799
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance
text: Incoming emails are rejected if they do not pass DMARC checks.

title: Control: ism-1234
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Email content filtering
text: Email content filtering is implemented to filter potentially harmful content in email bodies and attachments.

title: Control: ism-1502
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Blocking suspicious emails
text: Emails arriving via an external connection where the email source address uses an internal domain, or internal subdomain, are blocked at the email gateway.

title: Control: ism-1024
section: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Notifications of undeliverable emails
text: Notifications of undeliverable emails are only sent to senders that can be verified via SPF or other trusted means.

title: Control: ism-0518
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network documentation
text: Network documentation is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0516
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network documentation
text: Network documentation includes high-level network diagrams showing all connections into networks and logical network diagrams showing all critical servers, high-value servers, network devices and network security appliances.

title: Control: ism-1912
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network documentation
text: Network documentation includes device settings for all critical servers, high-value servers, network devices and network security appliances.

title: Control: ism-1178
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network documentation
text: Network documentation provided to a third party, or published in public tender documentation, only contains details necessary for other parties to undertake contractual services.

title: Control: ism-1181
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network segmentation and segregation
text: Networks are segregated into multiple network zones according to the criticality of servers, services and data.

title: Control: ism-1577
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network segmentation and segregation
text: An organisation’s networks are segregated from their service providers’ networks.

title: Control: ism-1532
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using virtual local area networks
text: VLANs are not used to separate network traffic between an organisation’s networks and public network infrastructure.

title: Control: ism-0529
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using virtual local area networks
text: VLANs are not used to separate network traffic between networks belonging to different security domains.

title: Control: ism-0530
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using virtual local area networks
text: Network devices managing VLANs are administered from the most trusted security domain.

title: Control: ism-0535
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using virtual local area networks
text: Network devices managing VLANs belonging to different security domains do not share VLAN trunks.

title: Control: ism-1364
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using virtual local area networks
text: Network devices managing VLANs terminate VLANs belonging to different security domains on separate physical network interfaces.

title: Control: ism-2068
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Functional separation between networked devices and the internet
text: Internet connectivity for networked devices is strictly limited to those that require access.

title: Control: ism-1863
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Networked management interfaces
text: Networked management interfaces for IT equipment are not directly exposed to the internet.

title: Control: ism-2160
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Networked management interfaces
text: Networked management interfaces for IT equipment are only accessible from a dedicated management network that is segregated from the wider network and the internet.

title: Control: ism-0385
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Functional separation between servers
text: Servers maintain effective functional separation from each other.

title: Control: ism-1479
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Functional separation between servers
text: Servers minimise communications with other servers at the network and file system level.

title: Control: ism-1781
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network encryption
text: All data communicated over network infrastructure is encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.

title: Control: ism-1186
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using Internet Protocol version 6
text: IPv6 capable network security appliances are used on IPv6 and dual-stack networks.

title: Control: ism-1428
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using Internet Protocol version 6
text: Unless explicitly required, IPv6 tunnelling is disabled on all network devices.

title: Control: ism-1429
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using Internet Protocol version 6
text: IPv6 tunnelling is blocked by network security appliances at externally connected network boundaries.

title: Control: ism-1430
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using Internet Protocol version 6
text: Dynamically assigned IPv6 addresses are configured with Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol version 6 in a stateful manner with lease data stored in a centralised event logging facility.

title: Control: ism-0520
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network access controls
text: Network access controls are implemented on networks to prevent the connection of unauthorised network devices and networked IT equipment.

title: Control: ism-1182
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network access controls
text: Network access controls are implemented to limit the flow of network traffic within and between network segments to only that required for business purposes.

title: Control: ism-1321
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / 802.1X authentication and key exchange
text: 802.1X with EAP-TLS is used for mutual authentication and key exchange; with all other EAP methods disabled on supplicants and authentication servers.

title: Control: ism-1711
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / 802.1X authentication and key exchange
text: User identity confidentiality is used if available with EAP-TLS implementations.

title: Control: ism-1322
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Evaluation of 802.1X implementations
text: Evaluated supplicants, authenticators and authentication servers are used for 802.1X authentication implementations.

title: Control: ism-1323
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Generating and issuing X.509 certificates for authentication
text: X.509 certificates are required for devices and human users authenticating to networks using 802.1X.

title: Control: ism-1324
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Generating and issuing X.509 certificates for authentication
text: X.509 certificates are generated using an evaluated certificate authority or hardware security module.

title: Control: ism-1327
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Generating and issuing X.509 certificates for authentication
text: X.509 certificates are protected by logical and physical access controls and encryption, with those issued to human users requiring authentication before use.

title: Control: ism-1454
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service authentication
text: Communications between authenticators and a RADIUS server are encapsulated with an additional layer of encryption using RADIUS over Internet Protocol Security or RADIUS over Transport Layer Security.

title: Control: ism-1006
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network management traffic
text: Security measures are implemented to prevent unauthorised access to network management traffic.

title: Control: ism-1962
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using the Server Message Block protocol
text: SMB version 1 is not used on networks.

title: Control: ism-1311
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using the Simple Network Management Protocol
text: SNMP version 1 and SNMP version 2 are not used on networks.

title: Control: ism-1312
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using the Simple Network Management Protocol
text: All default SNMP community strings on network devices are changed and write access is disabled.

title: Control: ism-1028
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using network-based intrusion detection and prevention systems
text: A NIDS or NIPS is deployed in gateways between an organisation’s networks and other networks they do not manage.

title: Control: ism-1030
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using network-based intrusion detection and prevention systems
text: A NIDS or NIPS is located immediately inside the outermost firewall for gateways and configured to generate event logs and alerts for network traffic that contravenes any rule in a firewall ruleset.

title: Control: ism-1627
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Blocking anonymity network traffic
text: Inbound network connections from anonymity networks are blocked.

title: Control: ism-1628
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Blocking anonymity network traffic
text: Outbound network connections to anonymity networks are blocked.

title: Control: ism-2017
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Encrypted Domain Name System Services
text: DNS traffic is encrypted by clients and servers using ASD-approved cryptography.

title: Control: ism-1782
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Protective Domain Name System Services
text: A protective DNS service is used to block access to known malicious domain names.

title: Control: ism-1800
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network device integrity
text: Network devices are flashed with trusted firmware before they are used for the first time.

title: Control: ism-2161
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network device integrity
text: The integrity of network device firmware and running configurations is verified against an approved known-good baseline following patching, on detection of anomalous behaviour and at least monthly.

title: Control: ism-1304
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network device hardening
text: Default user accounts or credentials for network devices, including for any pre-configured user accounts, are changed, disabled or removed during initial setup.

title: Control: ism-2162
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network device hardening
text: Unneeded components, services and functionality of network devices are disabled or removed.

title: Control: ism-0534
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Disabling unused physical ports on network devices
text: Unused physical ports on network devices are disabled.

title: Control: ism-1801
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Regularly restarting network devices
text: Network devices are restarted at least monthly.

title: Control: ism-1963
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network device event logging
text: Security-relevant events for internet-facing network devices are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-1964
section: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network device event logging
text: Security-relevant events for non-internet-facing network devices are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-2163
section: Guidelines for networking / Wired networks / Media Access Control Security
text: When using MACsec, confidentiality protection mode is enabled using GCM-AES-128, GCM-AES-256, GCM-AES-XPN-128 or GCM-AES-XPN-256, preferably GCM-AES-256 or GCM-AES-XPN-256.

title: Control: ism-2164
section: Guidelines for networking / Wired networks / Media Access Control Security
text: A connectivity association lifetime of less than 24 hours (86400 seconds) is used for MACsec connections.

title: Control: ism-2165
section: Guidelines for networking / Wired networks / Media Access Control Security
text: When using EAP-TLS, each device performs a fresh EAP-TLS authentication each time a new Connectivity Association Key is required.

title: Control: ism-2166
section: Guidelines for networking / Wired networks / Media Access Control Security
text: A secure association lifetime of less than four hours (14400 seconds) is used for MACsec connections.

title: Control: ism-2167
section: Guidelines for networking / Wired networks / Media Access Control Security
text: The use of a Pre-Shared Key as a fallback authentication method for MACsec is disabled.

title: Control: ism-1314
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Choosing wireless devices
text: All wireless devices are Wi-Fi Alliance certified.

title: Control: ism-0536
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Public wireless networks
text: Public wireless networks provided for public use are segregated from all other organisation networks.

title: Control: ism-1315
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Administrative interfaces for wireless access points
text: The administrative interface on wireless access points is disabled for wireless network connections.

title: Control: ism-1710
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Default settings
text: Settings for wireless access points are hardened.

title: Control: ism-1316
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Default settings
text: Default SSIDs of wireless access points are changed.

title: Control: ism-1317
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Default settings
text: SSIDs of non-public wireless networks are not readily associated with an organisation, the location of their premises or the functionality of wireless networks.

title: Control: ism-1318
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Default settings
text: SSID broadcasting is not disabled on wireless access points.

title: Control: ism-1320
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Media Access Control address filtering
text: MAC address filtering is not used to restrict which devices can connect to wireless networks.

title: Control: ism-1319
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Static addressing
text: Static addressing is not used for assigning IP addresses on wireless networks.

title: Control: ism-1332
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Confidentiality and integrity of wireless network traffic
text: WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit mode is used to protect the confidentiality and integrity of all wireless network traffic.

title: Control: ism-1330
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Caching 802.1X authentication outcomes
text: The PMK caching period is not set to greater than 1440 minutes (24 hours).

title: Control: ism-1712
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Fast Basic Service Set Transition
text: The use of FT (802.11r) is disabled unless authenticator-to-authenticator communications are secured by an ASD-Approved Cryptographic Protocol.

title: Control: ism-1334
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Interference between wireless networks
text: Wireless networks implement sufficient frequency separation from other wireless networks.

title: Control: ism-1335
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Protecting management frames on wireless networks
text: Wireless access points enable the use of the 802.11w amendment to protect management frames.

title: Control: ism-1338
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Wireless network footprint
text: Instead of deploying a small number of wireless access points that broadcast on high power, a greater number of wireless access points that use less broadcast power are deployed to achieve the desired footprint for wireless networks.

title: Control: ism-1013
section: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Wireless network footprint
text: The effective range of wireless communications outside an organisation’s area of control is limited by implementing RF shielding on facilities in which SECRET or TOP SECRET wireless networks are used.

title: Control: ism-1437
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Cloud-based hosting of online services
text: Cloud service providers are used for hosting online services.

title: Control: ism-1579
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Capacity and availability planning and monitoring for online services
text: Cloud service providers’ ability to scale resources dynamically in response to genuine spikes in demand is discussed and verified as part of capacity and availability planning for online services.

title: Control: ism-1580
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Capacity and availability planning and monitoring for online services
text: Where a high availability requirement exists for online services, the services are architected to automatically transition between availability zones.

title: Control: ism-1581
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Capacity and availability planning and monitoring for online services
text: Continuous real-time monitoring of the capacity and availability of online services is performed.

title: Control: ism-1438
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Using content delivery networks
text: Where a high availability requirement exists for website hosting, CDNs that cache websites are used.

title: Control: ism-1439
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Using content delivery networks
text: If using CDNs, disclosing the IP addresses of web servers under an organisation’s control (referred to as origin servers) is avoided and access to the origin servers is restricted to the CDNs and authorised management networks.

title: Control: ism-1431
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Denial-of-service attack mitigation strategies
text:
Denial-of-service attack mitigation strategies are discussed with cloud service providers, specifically:

- their capacity to withstand denial-of-service attacks
- costs likely to be incurred as a result of denial-of-service attacks
- availability monitoring and thresholds for notification of denial-of-service attacks
- thresholds for turning off any online services or functionality during denial-of-service attacks
- pre-approved actions that can be undertaken during denial-of-service attacks
- any arrangements with upstream service providers to block malicious network traffic as far upstream as possible.

title: Control: ism-1436
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Denial-of-service attack mitigation strategies
text: Critical online services are segregated from other online services that are more likely to be targeted as part of denial-of-service attacks.

title: Control: ism-1432
section: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Denial-of-service attack mitigation strategies
text: Domain names for online services are protected via registrar locking and confirming that domain registration details are correct.

title: Control: ism-0499
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Communications security doctrine
text: Communications security doctrine and policy produced by ASD for the management and operation of HACE is complied with.

title: Control: ism-1802
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / High Assurance Cryptographic Equipment
text: HACE are issued an Approval for Use by ASD and operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated Australian Communications Security Instructions.

title: Control: ism-0507
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic key management processes and procedures
text: Cryptographic key management processes, and supporting cryptographic key management procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-0457
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic implementation assurance
text: Cryptographic equipment, applications or libraries that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against an ASD-endorsed Protection Profile are used when encrypting media that contains OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED data.

title: Control: ism-0460
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic implementation assurance
text: HACE is used when encrypting media that contains SECRET or TOP SECRET data.

title: Control: ism-0465
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic implementation assurance
text: Cryptographic equipment, applications or libraries that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against an ASD-endorsed Protection Profile are used to protect OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED data when communicated over insufficiently secure networks, outside of appropriately secure areas or via public network infrastructure.

title: Control: ism-0467
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic implementation assurance
text: HACE is used to protect SECRET and TOP SECRET data when communicated over insufficiently secure networks, outside of appropriately secure areas or via public network infrastructure.

title: Control: ism-0455
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Data recovery
text: Where practical, cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries provide a means of data recovery to allow for circumstances where the encryption key is unavailable due to loss, damage or failure.

title: Control: ism-0462
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Handling encrypted IT equipment and media
text: When a user authenticates to the encryption functionality of IT equipment or media, it is treated in accordance with its original sensitivity or classification until the user deauthenticates from the encryption functionality.

title: Control: ism-0501
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Transporting cryptographic equipment
text: Keyed cryptographic equipment is transported based on the sensitivity or classification of its keying material.

title: Control: ism-0142
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Reporting cryptographic-related cyber security incidents
text: The compromise or suspected compromise of cryptographic equipment or associated keying material is reported to the chief information security officer, or one of their delegates, as soon as possible after it occurs.

title: Control: ism-1091
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Reporting cryptographic-related cyber security incidents
text: Keying material is changed when compromised or suspected of being compromised.

title: Control: ism-1080
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using cryptographic algorithms
text: An AACA or high assurance cryptographic algorithm is used when encrypting data at rest.

title: Control: ism-0471
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using cryptographic algorithms
text: Only AACAs or high assurance cryptographic algorithms are used by cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries.

title: Control: ism-0994
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Asymmetric cryptographic algorithms
text: ECDH is used in preference to DH.

title: Control: ism-0472
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Diffie-Hellman
text: When using DH for agreeing on encryption session keys, a modulus of at least 2048 bits is used, preferably 3072 bits.

title: Control: ism-1759
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Diffie-Hellman
text: When using DH for agreeing on encryption session keys, a modulus of at least 3072 bits is used, preferably 3072 bits.

title: Control: ism-1629
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Diffie-Hellman
text: When using DH for agreeing on encryption session keys, a modulus and associated parameters are selected according to NIST SP 800-56A Rev. 3.

title: Control: ism-1446
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Elliptic Curve Cryptography
text: When using elliptic curve cryptography, a suitable curve from NIST SP 800-186 is used.

title: Control: ism-0474
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman
text: When using ECDH for agreeing on encryption session keys, a base point order and key size of at least 224 bits is used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.

title: Control: ism-1761
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman
text: When using ECDH for agreeing on encryption session keys, NIST P-256, P-384 or P-521 curves are used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.

title: Control: ism-1762
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman
text: When using ECDH for agreeing on encryption session keys, NIST P-384 or P-521 curves are used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.

title: Control: ism-0475
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm
text: When using ECDSA for digital signatures, a base point order and key size of at least 224 bits is used, preferably the P-384 curve.

title: Control: ism-1763
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm
text: When using ECDSA for digital signatures, NIST P-256, P-384 or P-521 curves are used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.

title: Control: ism-1764
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm
text: When using ECDSA for digital signatures, NIST P-384 or P-521 curves are used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.

title: Control: ism-1990
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using post-quantum cryptographic algorithms
text: When using ML-DSA and ML-KEM, as per FIPS 204 and FIPS 203 respectively, adherence to pre-requisite FIPS 140-3 validation is preferred.

title: Control: ism-1991
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm
text: When using ML-DSA for digital signatures, ML-DSA-65 or ML-DSA-87 is used, preferably ML-DSA-87.

title: Control: ism-1992
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm
text: When using ML-DSA for digital signatures, the hedged variant is used whenever possible.

title: Control: ism-1993
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm
text: Pre-hashed variants of ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 are only used when the performance of default variants is unacceptable.

title: Control: ism-1994
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm
text: When the pre-hashed variants of ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 are used, at least SHA-384 and SHA-512 respectively are used for pre-hashing.

title: Control: ism-1995
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism
text: When using ML-KEM for encapsulating encryption session keys (and similar keys), ML-KEM-768 or ML-KEM-1024 is used, preferably ML-KEM-1024.

title: Control: ism-0476
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Rivest-Shamir-Adleman
text: When using RSA for digital signatures, and transporting encryption session keys (and similar keys), a modulus of at least 2048 bits is used, preferably 3072 bits.

title: Control: ism-1765
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Rivest-Shamir-Adleman
text: When using RSA for digital signatures, and transporting encryption session keys (and similar keys), a modulus of at least 3072 bits is used, preferably 3072 bits.

title: Control: ism-0477
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Rivest-Shamir-Adleman
text: When using RSA for digital signatures, and for transporting encryption session keys (and similar keys), a different key pair is used for digital signatures and transporting encryption session keys.

title: Control: ism-1766
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Secure Hashing Algorithms
text: When using SHA-2 for hashing, an output size of at least 224 bits is used, preferably SHA-384 or SHA-512.

title: Control: ism-1767
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Secure Hashing Algorithms
text: When using SHA-2 for hashing, an output size of at least 256 bits is used, preferably SHA-384 or SHA-512.

title: Control: ism-1768
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Secure Hashing Algorithms
text: When using SHA-2 for hashing, an output size of at least 384 bits is used, preferably SHA-384 or SHA-512.

title: Control: ism-1769
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using symmetric cryptographic algorithms
text: When using AES for encryption, AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256 is used, preferably AES-256.

title: Control: ism-1770
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using symmetric cryptographic algorithms
text: When using AES for encryption, AES-192 or AES-256 is used, preferably AES-256.

title: Control: ism-0479
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using symmetric cryptographic algorithms
text: Symmetric cryptographic algorithms are not used in Electronic Codebook Mode.

title: Control: ism-2073
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Transitioning to post-quantum cryptography
text: A post-quantum cryptography transition plan is developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1917
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Transitioning to post-quantum cryptography
text: The development and procurement of new cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries ensures support for the use of ML-DSA-87, ML-KEM-1024, SHA-384, SHA-512 and AES-256 by no later than 2030.

title: Control: ism-1996
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Post-quantum traditional hybrid schemes
text: When a post-quantum traditional hybrid scheme is used, either the post-quantum cryptographic algorithm, the traditional cryptographic algorithm or both are AACAs.

title: Control: ism-0469
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic protocols / Using cryptographic protocols
text: An AACP or high assurance cryptographic protocol is used when encrypting data in transit.

title: Control: ism-0481
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic protocols / Using cryptographic protocols
text: Only AACPs or high assurance cryptographic protocols are used by cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries.

title: Control: ism-0494
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Mode of operation
text: Tunnel mode is used for IPsec connections; however, if using transport mode, an IP tunnel is used.

title: Control: ism-0496
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Protocol selection
text: The ESP protocol is used for authentication and encryption of IPsec connections.

title: Control: ism-1233
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Key exchange
text: IKE version 2 is used for key exchange when establishing IPsec connections.

title: Control: ism-1771
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Encryption algorithms
text: AES is used for encrypting IPsec connections, preferably ENCR_AES_GCM_16.

title: Control: ism-1772
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Pseudorandom function
text: PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256, PRF_HMAC_SHA2_384 or PRF_HMAC_SHA2_512 is used for IPsec connections, preferably PRF_HMAC_SHA2_512.

title: Control: ism-0998
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Integrity algorithms
text: AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_384_192, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_512_256 or NONE (only with AES-GCM) is used for authenticating IPsec connections, preferably NONE.

title: Control: ism-0999
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Diffie-Hellman groups
text: DH or ECDH is used for key establishment of IPsec connections, preferably 384-bit random ECP group, 3072-bit MODP Group or 4096-bit MODP Group.

title: Control: ism-0498
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Security association lifetimes
text: A security association lifetime of less than four hours (14400 seconds) is used for IPsec connections.

title: Control: ism-1000
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Perfect Forward Secrecy
text: PFS is used for IPsec connections.

title: Control: ism-1506
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Configuring Secure Shell
text: The use of SSH version 1 is disabled for SSH connections.

title: Control: ism-0484
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Configuring Secure Shell
text:
The SSH daemon is configured to:

- only listen on the required interfaces (ListenAddress xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx)
- have a suitable login banner (Banner x)
- have a login authentication timeout of no more than 60 seconds (LoginGraceTime 60)
- disable host-based authentication (HostbasedAuthentication no)
- disable rhosts-based authentication (IgnoreRhosts yes)
- disable the ability to log in directly as root (PermitRootLogin no)
- disable empty passwords (PermitEmptyPasswords no)
- disable connection forwarding (AllowTCPForwarding no)
- disable gateway ports (GatewayPorts no)
- disable X11 forwarding (X11Forwarding no).

title: Control: ism-0485
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Authentication mechanisms
text: Public key-based authentication is used for SSH connections.

title: Control: ism-1449
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Authentication mechanisms
text: SSH private keys are protected with a password or a key encryption key.

title: Control: ism-0487
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Automated remote access
text:
When using logins without a password for SSH connections, the following are disabled:

- access from IP addresses that do not require access
- port forwarding
- agent credential forwarding
- X11 forwarding
- console access.

title: Control: ism-0488
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Automated remote access
text: If using remote access without the use of a password for SSH connections, the ‘forced command’ option is used to specify what command is executed and parameter checking is enabled.

title: Control: ism-0489
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / SSH-agent
text: When SSH-agent or similar key caching applications are used, cached private keys have a maximum lifetime of four hours and, where applicable, screen locks are used on workstations and servers.

title: Control: ism-0490
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions / Configuring Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions
text: Versions of S/MIME earlier than S/MIME version 3.0 are not used for S/MIME connections.

title: Control: ism-1139
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: Only the latest version of TLS is used for TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-1369
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: AES-GCM is used for encryption of TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-1370
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: Only server-initiated secure renegotiation is used for TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-1372
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: The ephemeral variant of DH or ECDH is used for key establishment of TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-1373
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: Anonymous DH is not used for TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-1374
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: SHA-2-based certificates are used for TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-1375
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: SHA-2 is used for the Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) and pseudorandom function (PRF) for TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-1553
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: TLS compression is disabled for TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-1453
section: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security
text: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) is used for TLS connections.

title: Control: ism-0628
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways
text: Gateways are implemented between networks belonging to different security domains.

title: Control: ism-0637
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways
text: Gateways implement a demilitarised zone if external parties require access to an organisation’s services.

title: Control: ism-0631
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways
text: Gateways only allow explicitly authorised data flows.

title: Control: ism-1192
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways
text: Gateways inspect and filter data flows at the transport and above network layers.

title: Control: ism-1427
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways
text: Gateways perform ingress traffic filtering to detect and prevent IP source address spoofing.

title: Control: ism-1520
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways
text: System administrators for gateways undergo appropriate employment screening, and where necessary hold an appropriate security clearance, based on the sensitivity or classification of gateways.

title: Control: ism-0613
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways
text: System administrators for gateways that connect to Australian Eyes Only or Releasable To networks are Australian nationals.

title: Control: ism-1773
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways
text: System administrators for gateways that connect to Australian Government Access Only networks are Australian nationals or seconded foreign nationals.

title: Control: ism-0611
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways
text: System administrators for gateways are assigned the minimum privileges required to perform their duties.

title: Control: ism-0616
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways
text: Separation of duties is implemented in performing administrative activities for gateways.

title: Control: ism-0612
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways
text: System administrators for gateways are formally trained on the operation and management of gateways.

title: Control: ism-1774
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administration of gateways
text: Gateways are managed via a secure path isolated from all connected networks.

title: Control: ism-0629
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administration of gateways
text: For gateways between networks belonging to different security domains, any shared components are managed by system administrators for the higher security domain or by system administrators from a mutually agreed upon third party.

title: Control: ism-0619
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Authenticating to networks accessed via gateways
text: Users authenticate to other networks accessed via gateways.

title: Control: ism-0622
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Authenticating to networks accessed via gateways
text: IT equipment authenticates to other networks accessed via gateways.

title: Control: ism-1783
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Border Gateway Protocol routing security
text: Public IP addresses controlled by, or used by, an organisation are signed by valid ROA records.

title: Control: ism-2018
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Border Gateway Protocol routing security
text: Routes for RPKI-registered IP addresses that are advertised from invalid Autonomous Systems, or that are longer than allowed, are rejected or deprioritised by routers that exchange routes via BGP.

title: Control: ism-0634
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Gateway event logging
text:
Security-relevant events for gateways are centrally logged, including:

- data packets and data flows permitted through gateways
- data packets and data flows attempting to leave gateways
- real-time alerts for attempted intrusions.

title: Control: ism-1037
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Assessment of gateways
text: Gateways undergo testing following configuration changes, and at regular intervals no more than six months apart, to validate that they conform to expected security configurations.

title: Control: ism-0100
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Assessment of gateways
text: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET gateways undergo an IRAP assessment, using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the IRAP assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

title: Control: ism-2019
section: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Assessment of gateways
text: TOP SECRET gateways undergo a security control assessment by ASD assessors (or their delegates), using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

title: Control: ism-0626
section: Guidelines for gateways / Cross domain solutions / Implementing cross domain solutions
text: CDSs are implemented between SECRET or TOP SECRET networks and any other networks belonging to different security domains.

title: Control: ism-0597
section: Guidelines for gateways / Cross domain solutions / Consultation on cross domain solutions
text: When planning, designing, implementing or introducing additional connectivity to CDSs, ASD is consulted and any directions provided by ASD are complied with.

title: Control: ism-0635
section: Guidelines for gateways / Cross domain solutions / Separation of data flows
text: CDSs implement isolated upward and downward network paths.

title: Control: ism-1522
section: Guidelines for gateways / Cross domain solutions / Separation of data flows
text: CDSs implement independent security-enforcing functions for upward and downward network paths.

title: Control: ism-1521
section: Guidelines for gateways / Cross domain solutions / Separation of data flows
text: CDSs implement protocol breaks at each network layer.

title: Control: ism-0610
section: Guidelines for gateways / Cross domain solutions / Cross domain solution use
text: Human users are trained on the secure use of CDSs before access is granted.

title: Control: ism-0670
section: Guidelines for gateways / Cross domain solutions / Cross domain solution event logging
text: Security-relevant events for CDSs are centrally logged.

title: Control: ism-1523
section: Guidelines for gateways / Cross domain solutions / Cross domain solution event logging
text: A sample of security-relevant events relating to data transfer policies are taken at least every three months and assessed against security policies for CDSs to identify any operational failures.

title: Control: ism-1528
section: Guidelines for gateways / Firewalls / Using firewalls
text: Evaluated firewalls are used between an organisation’s networks and public network infrastructure.

title: Control: ism-0639
section: Guidelines for gateways / Firewalls / Using firewalls
text: Evaluated firewalls are used between networks belonging to different security domains.

title: Control: ism-1862
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web application firewalls / Using web application firewalls
text: If using a WAF, disclosing the IP addresses of web servers under an organisation’s control (referred to as origin servers) is avoided and access to the origin servers is restricted to the WAF and authorised management networks.

title: Control: ism-0643
section: Guidelines for gateways / Diodes / Using diodes
text: Evaluated diodes are used for controlling the data flow of unidirectional gateways between an organisation’s networks and public network infrastructure.

title: Control: ism-0645
section: Guidelines for gateways / Diodes / Using diodes
text: Evaluated diodes used for controlling the data flow of unidirectional gateways between SECRET or TOP SECRET networks and public network infrastructure complete a high assurance evaluation.

title: Control: ism-1157
section: Guidelines for gateways / Diodes / Using diodes
text: Evaluated diodes are used for controlling the data flow of unidirectional gateways between networks.

title: Control: ism-1158
section: Guidelines for gateways / Diodes / Using diodes
text: Evaluated diodes used for controlling the data flow of unidirectional gateways between SECRET or TOP SECRET networks and any other networks complete a high assurance evaluation.

title: Control: ism-0260
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web proxies / Using web proxies
text: All web access, including that by internal servers, is conducted through web proxies.

title: Control: ism-0261
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web proxies / Web proxy event logging
text:
The following details are centrally logged for websites accessed via web proxies:

- web address
- date and time
- user
- amount of data uploaded and downloaded
- internal and external IP addresses.

title: Control: ism-0963
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Using web content filters
text: Web content filtering is implemented to filter potentially harmful web-based content.

title: Control: ism-0961
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Using web content filters
text: Client-side active content is restricted by web content filters to an organisation-approved list of domain names.

title: Control: ism-1237
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Using web content filters
text: Web content filtering is applied to outbound web traffic where appropriate.

title: Control: ism-0263
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Transport Layer Security filtering
text: TLS traffic communicated through gateways is decrypted and inspected.

title: Control: ism-0958
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Allowing and blocking access to domain names
text: An organisation-approved list of domain names, or list of website categories, is implemented for all Hypertext Transfer Protocol and Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure traffic communicated through gateways.

title: Control: ism-1236
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Allowing and blocking access to domain names
text: Malicious domain names, dynamic domain names and domain names that can be registered anonymously for free are blocked by web content filters.

title: Control: ism-1171
section: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Allowing and blocking access to domain names
text: Attempts to access websites through their IP addresses instead of their domain names are blocked by web content filters.

title: Control: ism-0659
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Performing content filtering
text: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content filtering checks.

title: Control: ism-0651
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Performing content filtering
text: Files identified by content filtering checks as malicious, or that cannot be inspected, are blocked.

title: Control: ism-0652
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Performing content filtering
text: Files identified by content filtering checks as suspicious are quarantined until reviewed and subsequently approved or not approved for release.

title: Control: ism-1524
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Performing content filtering
text: Content filters used by CDSs undergo rigorous security testing to ensure they perform as expected and cannot be bypassed.

title: Control: ism-1293
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Encrypted files
text: Encrypted files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs are decrypted to undergo content filtering checks.

title: Control: ism-1289
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Archive files
text: Archive files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs are unpacked to undergo content filtering checks.

title: Control: ism-1290
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Archive files
text: Archive files are unpacked in a controlled manner to ensure content filter performance or availability is not adversely affected.

title: Control: ism-1288
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Antivirus scanning
text: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo antivirus scanning using multiple different scanning engines.

title: Control: ism-1389
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Automated dynamic analysis
text: Executable files imported via gateways or CDSs are automatically executed in a sandbox to detect any suspicious behaviour.

title: Control: ism-0649
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Allowing specific content types
text: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs are filtered for allowed file types.

title: Control: ism-1284
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Content validation
text: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content validation.

title: Control: ism-1965
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Content checking
text: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content checking.

title: Control: ism-1286
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Content conversion
text: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content conversion.

title: Control: ism-1287
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Content sanitisation
text: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content sanitisation.

title: Control: ism-0677
section: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Validating file integrity
text: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs that have a digital signature or cryptographic checksum are validated.

title: Control: ism-0591
section: Guidelines for gateways / Peripheral switches / Using peripheral switches
text: Evaluated peripheral switches are used when sharing peripherals between systems.

title: Control: ism-1457
section: Guidelines for gateways / Peripheral switches / Using peripheral switches
text: Evaluated peripheral switches used for sharing peripherals between SECRET and TOP SECRET systems, or between SECRET or TOP SECRET systems belonging to different security domains, preferably complete a high assurance evaluation.

title: Control: ism-1480
section: Guidelines for gateways / Peripheral switches / Using peripheral switches
text: Evaluated peripheral switches used for sharing peripherals between SECRET or TOP SECRET systems and any non-SECRET or TOP SECRET systems complete a high assurance evaluation.

title: Control: ism-0663
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Data transfer processes and procedures
text: Data transfer processes, and supporting data transfer procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

title: Control: ism-1535
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Data transfer processes and procedures
text: Processes, and supporting procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained to prevent AUSTEO, AGAO and REL data in textual and non-textual formats from being exported to unsuitable foreign systems.

title: Control: ism-0661
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Accountability for data transfers
text: Human users transferring data to and from systems are held accountable for data transfers they perform.

title: Control: ism-0657
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual import of data
text: When manually importing data to systems, the data is scanned for malicious and active content.

title: Control: ism-1778
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual import of data
text: When manually importing data to systems, all data that fails security checks is quarantined until reviewed and subsequently approved or not approved for release.

title: Control: ism-0664
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Authorising export of data
text: Data exported from SECRET and TOP SECRET systems is reviewed and authorised by a trustworthy source beforehand.

title: Control: ism-0675
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Authorising export of data
text: Data authorised for export from SECRET and TOP SECRET systems is digitally signed by a trustworthy source.

title: Control: ism-0665
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Authorising export of data
text: Trustworthy sources for SECRET and TOP SECRET systems are limited to people and systems that have been verified and authorised as such by the chief information security officer.

title: Control: ism-1187
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual export of data
text: When manually exporting data from systems, the data is checked for unsuitable protective markings.

title: Control: ism-0669
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual export of data
text: When manually exporting data from SECRET and TOP SECRET systems, digital signatures are validated and keyword checks are performed within all textual data.

title: Control: ism-1779
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual export of data
text: When manually exporting data from systems, all data that fails security checks is quarantined until reviewed and subsequently approved or not approved for release.

title: Control: ism-1586
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Monitoring data import and export
text: Data transfer logs are used to record all data imports and exports from systems.

title: Control: ism-1294
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Monitoring data import and export
text: Data transfer logs for systems are partially verified at least monthly.

title: Control: ism-0660
section: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Monitoring data import and export
text: Data transfer logs for SECRET and TOP SECRET systems are fully verified at least monthly.
